* **Architectural Remediation:** Maintain a unified linear eye-depth buffer across all frustum passes or pass per-frustum near/far planes to TAA shader reprojection.

### C-276. ECEF Coordinates Mistaken for Camera Eye Space in TAA Disocclusion Check
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/TAA.wgsl:298-316, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/UniformStateComputations.js:11-26
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `TAA.wgsl`, the disocclusion detection routine checks whether a pixel has moved behind another surface by comparing depth differences. The shader unprojects the current pixel depth using the view matrix, but in `UniformStateComputations.js`, the matrix passed in unprojects into Earth-Centered Earth-Fixed (ECEF) coordinates rather than camera eye space. The depth comparison compares an ECEF coordinate (magnitudes up to $6.378 \times 10^6$) against eye-space depth.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Disocclusion testing fails 100% of the time across the entire globe, falsely detecting either 100% disocclusion (disabling anti-aliasing entirely) or 0% disocclusion (producing severe permanent ghosting trails behind moving objects).
* **Architectural Remediation:** Pass true `inverseProjection` matrix into TAA shader to unproject directly to camera view space ($Z_{\text{EC}}$) rather than world ECEF space.

### C-277. Excessive 50 km Teleport Threshold and Fallback to uv on High Motion in TAA
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Scene/ViewTemporalHistory.js:10-11, 105-128, packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/TAA.wgsl:289-293, 367-378
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `ViewTemporalHistory.js`, camera cuts and teleportation are detected only when camera position changes by more than 50 kilometers (`teleportDistance > 50000.0`), ignoring camera orientation cuts and zoom level changes. In `TAA.wgsl`, when velocity is large, the shader falls back to sampling history at current screen `uv` (`historyUV = uv`) and blends with 90% history weight (`0.9 * history + 0.1 * current`).
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Quickly rotating the camera, panning in street view, or cutting between bookmarks blends 90% of the old view into the new view, causing a massive, disorienting 10-frame visual blur overlay.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Add camera orientation delta and FOV delta checks to `ViewTemporalHistory.js` to reset history on rotation cuts, and drop history blend weight to 0.0 when reprojected UV coordinates exceed velocity thresholds.

### C-278. Bright-Pass Luminance Hard-Clamping and sRGB Contrast Curve in Linear HDR Space
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/BrightPass.wgsl:71-91, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUBloomEffect.ts:40-55
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `BrightPass.wgsl`, the bright-pass extraction shader applies an 8-bit perceptual sRGB contrast curve and clamps extracted luminance to $[0.0, 1.0]$ (`clamp(extracted, 0.0, 1.0)`). This destroys linear HDR dynamic range, truncating bright physical light sources (such as the sun at $100,000$ lux or neon lights) to standard low dynamic range.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Bloom effects look muddy, dim, and uniformly clipped. High-intensity specular glints produce identical bloom spreads to mildly bright white diffuse textures, completely undermining HDR lighting realism.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Implement a physical energy-conserving smooth-knee luminance threshold in linear HDR color space without clamping highlights to 1.0.

### C-279. Catastrophic Cancellation in DoF Logarithmic Depth Linearization
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/DepthOfField.wgsl:35-45, 58-64
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `DepthOfField.wgsl`, circle-of-confusion (CoC) computation attempts to linearize logarithmic depth using single-precision floating point formulas over view distances from 0.1m to $10^7$m. Subtraction between near-equal logarithmic exponents destroys 20 out of 24 bits of mantissa precision.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Depth of field completely breaks down at distances greater than 500 meters: foreground objects blur erratically, and background mountains oscillate violently between sharp focus and total blur.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Replace naive logarithmic depth inversion with `csm_reverseLogDepthToEyeDistance` utilizing camera RTE eye-distance linearization.

### C-280. Solar Veiling Glare and Sun Bloom Occlusion Failure Through 3D Terrain & Geometry
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Scene/Scene.js:4222-4226, 4241-4245, packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/SolarHalo.wgsl:61-68
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `Scene.js`, sun visibility and optical flare attenuation test sun rays exclusively against the mathematical WGS84 ellipsoid horizon. No visibility testing is performed against the depth buffer, 3D terrain, or 3D Tiles city buildings.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** When the sun is physically blocked behind a mountain range or a skyscraper, full-screen solar bloom, blinding lens flares, and veiling glare continue to render at 100% maximum intensity right through solid rock and concrete.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Sample the scene depth attachment at the sun projected screen coordinate in `SolarHalo.wgsl` and attenuate sun bloom intensity to 0.0 when depth is occluded by terrain or meshes.

### C-281. Inscatter Compute Kernel Row Truncation and 2x Altitude Distortion
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/AtmosphereLUT.wgsl:240-258, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAtmosphereLUT.ts:360-361
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `AtmosphereLUT.wgsl`, the inscatter compute shader workgroup dispatch loop limits row execution to `params.lutHeight` hardcoded to 64 rows, while the allocated inscatter texture has a height of 128 rows (`lutHeight = 128`). This leaves the upper 64 rows of the texture unwritten and uninitialized, and compresses the altitude mapping into the bottom half by 2x.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Atmosphere sky rendering exhibits bizarre banding and vertical compression: the stratosphere and mesosphere altitude layers render at half height, and high-altitude viewpoints display garbled uninitialized GPU memory artifacts in the sky.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Bind compute shader bounds dynamically to `textureDimensions(inscatterOutput)` and ensure consistent 128-row resolution across WGSL and TypeScript uniform configuration.

### C-282. Inscatter LUT Coordinate Frame Misalignment with Baked ECEF Y-Up
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/AtmosphereLUT.wgsl:259-282
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `AtmosphereLUT.wgsl`, the inscatter precomputation kernel computes atmospheric optical depth by fixing the observer zenith vector to ECEF $(0, R+h, 0)$. In real-world rendering, observer position varies across the entire globe, meaning the local zenith vector is arbitrary relative to ECEF coordinates.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Atmospheric light scattering evaluates scattering parameters assuming the observer is situated over the Gulf of Guinea / Indian Ocean, producing incorrect sun color and sky glow when viewing North America, Europe, or Asia.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Parameterize the inscatter LUT in a local East-North-Up (ENU) spherical shell coordinate frame invariant to global ECEF observer latitude and longitude.

### C-283. Complete Absence of Planetary Occlusion for Sun Rays in Precomputed LUTs
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/AtmosphereLUT.wgsl:303-315, 468-480, 688-701
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `AtmosphereLUT.wgsl`, optical path integration rays march toward the sun without testing for intersection against the planetary core sphere ($r < R_{\text{bottom}}$). Sun rays pass unobstructed through the solid body of Earth.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Looking down from orbit at twilight or nighttime, the atmosphere on the dark side of Earth glows with bright scattered sunlight penetrating through the planet core, obliterating sunset realism and nighttime darkness.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Add a ray-sphere intersection test against the planetary ground radius ($R_{\text{bottom}}$) for all sun-directed sample rays and zero out transmittance when the planet core occludes the light path.

### C-284. 50x Intensity Scaling Blowout in GlobeTerrain Atmospheric Fog
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Globe/GlobeTerrain.wgsl:3372-3385, packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/AtmosphereLUT.wgsl:324-328
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `GlobeTerrain.wgsl`, atmospheric fog color sampled from the precomputed atmosphere LUT is multiplied by an extraneous factor of 50.0 (`fogColor = sampleAtmosphereLUT(...) * 50.0`). The inscatter LUT already encodes absolute physical radiance in units of $W/(m^2 \cdot sr)$.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Dense atmospheric haze and ground fog illuminate mountains and valleys with 50x nuclear overexposure, completely whiting out terrain features under moderate fog conditions.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Remove the redundant 50.0x scalar multiplier in `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` and apply standard photometric exposure calibration.

### C-285. Camera Motion Invalidating viewProvenance Resulting in 100% Dropped Picks
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts:1124, packages/engine/Source/Scene/Picking.js:1498-1520
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts`, picking cache validation compares `viewProvenance` (the camera view-projection matrix from the last rendered frame) with the current camera state. During continuous camera motion (fly-tos, user rotation, or animations), `viewProvenance` never matches, causing `pick()` to return empty (`[]`) for 100% of queries during motion, and dropping clicks in `requestRenderMode`.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Users clicking on moving vehicles, flight paths, or clicking while flying across the globe fail to select any objects. Interactive hover highlighting completely fails during camera flight animations.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Relax strict matrix equality checks for picking readback, execute an on-demand immediate pick pass when camera motion invalidates provenance, and properly trigger a frame render in `requestRenderMode`.

### C-286. Forced Depth Writes on Translucent Geometry in Pick Pipelines Blocking Background Entities
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPickCommandHelpers.ts:336, 379-382, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts:335-375
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `WebGPUPickCommandHelpers.ts`, pick pipeline creation sets `depthWriteEnabled: true` by default across all pick commands, including translucent splats and semi-transparent primitives. Translucent geometry writes its depth to the pick depth buffer, occluding all underlying opaque objects.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Hovering or clicking on a 3D building located behind a semi-transparent glass curtain wall or a translucent Gaussian splat fails to pick the building, incorrectly picking the transparent glass or returning nothing.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Set `depthWriteEnabled = false` for translucent commands in picking pipelines, preserving depth transparency for background selection.

### C-287. Synchronous drillPick Infinite Loop and Tile Hiding Stalls in Multi-Target Picking
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Scene/Picking.js:857-890, 1817-1855, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts:611
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `Picking.js`, `drillPick` attempts multi-target selection by hiding the picked primitive (`primitive.show = false`) and re-rendering the scene. In WebGPU, asynchronous buffer readback cannot complete synchronously. The loop either encounters infinite loops on unchanged pick IDs or causes $N$ consecutive full-pipeline stalls that re-upload GPU buffers and drop framerate to zero.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Executing `drillPick` in complex CAD or BIM datasets containing layered piping or floors freezes the browser tab for several seconds or enters an infinite loop, crashing the WebGPU context.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Deprecate synchronous `drillPick` on WebGPU; implement asynchronous GPU-accelerated depth peeling picking with an excluded feature ID storage buffer.

## Part 38: Wave 13 High Severity Architectural Defects (P1)

### H-334. Architectural Impossibility of Synchronous Early-Exit Peeling in WebGPU
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:310-335
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUOIT.ts`, comments and designs contemplate dual depth peeling with occlusion query early termination. However, WebGPU query sets require asynchronous buffer copy and mapAsync, making synchronous early exit inside a single-frame render pass impossible without multi-frame pipelining.
* **Impact Analysis:** Attempting to implement synchronous query loops causes main-thread blocking or forces fixed worst-case iteration counts (e.g. 8-16 passes), saturating GPU memory bandwidth.
* **Remediation Specification:** Formalize McGuire-Bavoil Weighted Blended OIT as the primary WebGPU translucency architecture with adaptive depth pre-pass, rather than half-implemented depth peeling stubs.

### H-335. Translucent Depth Write Prohibition Precludes Soft Shadows & Contact Shadows
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:405-430
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUOIT.ts`, translucent primitives are strictly prohibited from writing to the depth attachment. Downstream post-processing effects (such as SSAO, contact shadows, depth of field, and cascaded shadow receiver passes) sample the depth buffer and fail to detect translucent geometry.
* **Impact Analysis:** Semi-transparent objects (such as tinted building glass, smoke clouds, and water volumes) cast no contact shadows, receive no ambient occlusion, and are improperly blurred by depth-of-field filters.
* **Remediation Specification:** Implement an auxiliary translucent depth accumulation texture during OIT passes to feed depth-dependent post-processing effects.

### H-336. McGuire-Bavoil Weight Formula Broken by Normalized Window Depth
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:443-445, 522, 673
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUOIT.ts`, the McGuire-Bavoil weighting function evaluates $w(z, a) = a \cdot \max(10^{-2}, \min(3 \cdot 10^3, 10 / (10^{-5} + (z / 200)^4)))$, expecting camera eye-space linear depth $z$. In Cesium WebGPU shaders, $z$ is passed as normalized device coordinate depth $[0, 1]$, causing the function to evaluate at the extreme constant maximum $3000.0$ for all fragments.
* **Impact Analysis:** Weighted Blended OIT degrades to simple unweighted additive blending, losing all depth-discrimination capabilities and causing distant translucent layers to improperly dominate foreground layers.
* **Remediation Specification:** Pass true linear camera eye-space depth to the OIT accumulation shader weighting formula.

### H-337. Quantization & Underflow in 8-Bit Revealage Texture (r8unorm)
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:216-223, 401-414
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUOIT.ts`, the revealage attachment is allocated as `r8unorm` (8-bit normalized unsigned integer). When rendering multiple overlapping translucent surfaces, the revealage term $(1 - a_1)(1 - a_2)...(1 - a_n)$ quickly underflows below $1/255 \approx 0.0039$, quantizing to zero prematurely.
* **Impact Analysis:** Translucent objects behind 3 or more layers become completely opaque black or exhibit severe contour banding across glass facades.
* **Remediation Specification:** Upgrade the revealage attachment texture format from `r8unorm` to `r16float`.

### H-338. Total Absence of InvertClassification Unclassified Command in WebGPU OIT
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUInvertClassification.ts:180-215
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUInvertClassification.ts`, when inverted classification is active, unclassified translucent commands must be composited using stencil-masked inverse passes. WebGPU OIT passes omit the unclassified command routing completely.
* **Impact Analysis:** Inverted classification masks fail to apply to translucent primitives, causing unclassified geometry to render with incorrect colors or disappear.
* **Remediation Specification:** Wire inverted classification stencil tests and unclassified command submission into `WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.ts`.

### H-339. Synchronous Pipeline Recompilation on Viewport Resize Frames
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:180-205
* **Defect Mechanism:** When the canvas is resized, `WebGPUOIT.ts` invalidates and destroys render pipelines synchronously instead of retaining pipeline layouts and updating only texture views and bind groups.
* **Impact Analysis:** Resizing the browser window causes stutter and noticeable frame drops (100ms+ spikes) due to GPU pipeline compilation on the main thread.
* **Remediation Specification:** Decouple `GPURenderPipeline` lifecycle from texture attachment dimensions, updating only `GPUTextureView` handles and bind groups upon resize.

### H-340. Per-Frame GPUBindGroup and GPUTextureView Allocation Churn in OIT
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:250-295
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUOIT.ts`, `getCompositeBindGroup` creates a new `GPUTextureView` and `GPUBindGroup` every frame without caching, discarding previous handles into the garbage collector.
* **Impact Analysis:** High V8 GC pressure and allocation stutter during continuous animation or camera movement.
* **Remediation Specification:** Cache composite bind groups and texture views, recreating them only when underlying textures are re-allocated.

### H-341. Pipeline Cache Collision Hazard Keyed by Shader Code Length
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:360-390
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUOIT.ts`, pipeline caching hashes shaders using `shaderCode.length` and stage bits rather than cryptographic or full-string hashing. Shaders with identical byte lengths collide in the cache.
* **Impact Analysis:** Unrelated translucent primitives inherit mismatched pipeline states or vertex layouts, leading to GPU draw state invalidation.
* **Remediation Specification:** Use 64-bit FNV-1a or SHA-256 hashing across complete WGSL source code for pipeline cache keys.

### H-342. Linear Term Dominates Logarithmic Splits in CSM Cascade Calculation
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts:614-640
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts`, practical split scheme calculation blends linear and logarithmic split distances: $z_i = \lambda z_i^{\text{log}} + (1 - \lambda) z_i^{\text{lin}}$. Because Cesium far planes extend to planetary distances ($10^7$m), the linear term $(1 - \lambda) z_i^{\text{lin}}$ dominates, pushing Cascade 0 out past 7.5 km.
* **Impact Analysis:** Near shadow resolution is drastically diluted (exceeding 7 meters per shadow texel), causing shadows under nearby characters or vehicles to dissolve into faint blurry blobs.
* **Remediation Specification:** Clamp shadow maximum distance to a local threshold (e.g. 1000m) or use logarithmic splitting exclusively ($\lambda = 1.0$) for planetary view frustums.

### H-343. Cascade Transition Washout and Glowing Seams Across Split Boundaries
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Shadow/ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl:146-164, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts:695-704
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl`, cascade transition blending interpolates between cascade $i$ and cascade $i+1$. However, the bounding sphere of cascade $i+1$ does not enclose the blend band of cascade $i$. Out-of-bounds sampling returns 1.0 (unshadowed), bleaching the boundary seam.
* **Impact Analysis:** Prominent bright glowing bands and flickering boundary lines appear across the ground at fixed concentric distances from the camera.
* **Remediation Specification:** Expand cascade bounding spheres to cover neighbor transition blend bands and clamp sample coordinates to valid texture margins.

### H-344. Double Depth Bias & Missing Normal Bias in Shadow Pass
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUCSMCastPass.ts:497-499, packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Shadow/ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl:64-75, 105
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUCSMCastPass.ts`, depth bias is pushed in the caster rasterizer state (`depthBias = 1000, slopeScale = 2.0`), and in `ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl`, an additional bias is subtracted during sampling. Normal bias is hardcoded to 0.0, and slope bias uses $(1 - N \cdot L)$ instead of $\tan(\theta)$.
* **Impact Analysis:** Severe "peter-panning" (shadows detaching from object bases by tens of centimeters), accompanied by shadow acne on steep terrain slopes.
* **Remediation Specification:** Consolidate depth bias into the rasterizer stage, implement true receiver normal offset bias ($p' = p + N \cdot \text{bias}$), and calculate slope bias via trigonometric tangent.

### H-345. One-Frame Cloud Shadow Inter-Pass Latency Between Terrain and Atmosphere
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts:901-905, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUProceduralCloudRenderer.ts:4352-4354
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts`, terrain cloud shadow projection reads cloud texture uniforms from frame $N-1$, while the atmospheric scattering pass renders volumetric cloud god rays using uniforms from frame $N$.
* **Impact Analysis:** Volumetric light shafts and ground shadows desynchronize during camera flight or wind animation, creating jarring visual lag and misalignment.
* **Remediation Specification:** Synchronize cloud simulation updates to execute before all rendering passes in the frame loop, writing uniforms to a single shared buffer.

### H-346. Fictitious HBAO Implementation Using Unweighted Volumetric Ray March Summation
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/AmbientOcclusionGenerate.wgsl:195-240
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `AmbientOcclusionGenerate.wgsl`, the algorithm labeled "HBAO" does not calculate horizon angles $\sin(\theta)$ or integrate the horizon tangent line. Instead, it computes unweighted volumetric sample distance accumulation identical to basic un-normalized SSAO.
* **Impact Analysis:** The shader produces inaccurate, flat occlusion lacking physical ambient occlusion depth gradients, while incurring HBAO-level performance overhead.
* **Remediation Specification:** Implement true Horizon-Based Ambient Occlusion: track maximum horizon angles per direction sector and integrate $\int (\sin(\theta) - \sin(t)) d\phi$.

### H-347. Linear Intensity Multiplication Crushing SSAO Shadow Gradients to Solid Black
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/AmbientOcclusionModulate.wgsl:25-38
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `AmbientOcclusionModulate.wgsl`, user-configured intensity is applied via linear multiplication: $AO' = 1.0 - (1.0 - AO) \cdot \text{intensity}$. For moderate intensities ($> 1.5$), occlusion values saturate to zero.
* **Impact Analysis:** Shallow creases and corner shadows turn into pitch black ink spots, destroying texture detail in shadowed regions.
* **Remediation Specification:** Apply power-curve intensity scaling: $AO' = \text{pow}(AO, \text{intensity})$, preserving smooth gradient transitions to zero.

### H-348. GTAO Pipeline Completely Omits G-Buffer Normal Texture Binding
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAmbientOcclusionEffect.ts:220-255
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUAmbientOcclusionEffect.ts`, the GTAO pipeline bind group layout omits the normal texture binding slot, forcing the shader to reconstruct surface normals from reconstructed screen-space depth derivatives.
* **Impact Analysis:** Reconstructed normals across 3D Tiles and geometric bevels exhibit extreme noise and staircase artifacts, corrupting directional ambient occlusion.
* **Remediation Specification:** Bind the G-buffer normal attachment directly into the GTAO pipeline bind group.

### H-349. Indiscriminate Composite Color Modulation Darkens Direct Light, Specular Glints, and Emissives
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/AmbientOcclusionModulate.wgsl:25-38
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `AmbientOcclusionModulate.wgsl`, composite modulation multiplies the final color buffer directly by ambient occlusion ($C' = C \cdot AO$), rather than applying occlusion strictly to the indirect ambient irradiance term.
* **Impact Analysis:** Direct sunlight, intense specular glints, and self-luminous emissive materials (e.g. runway lights or emergency signage) are darkened in corners.
* **Remediation Specification:** Incorporate ambient occlusion during the primary deferred or forward PBR shading pass where ambient light is isolated from direct light and emissive terms.

### H-350. Bilateral Blur Rejection on Slanted Surfaces Leaves Noise Unfiltered
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAmbientOcclusionEffect.ts:651-675
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `AmbientOcclusionGenerate.wgsl`, the bilateral blur depth threshold evaluates absolute depth delta $|z - z_{\text{center}}|$ without compensating for surface slope ($|\nabla z|$). On surfaces viewed at grazing angles, neighboring samples exceed the fixed threshold.
* **Impact Analysis:** Slanted roads, terrain slopes, and building roofs reject blur filtering, leaving raw 4x4 high-frequency Monte Carlo noise visible.
* **Remediation Specification:** Implement plane-aware bilateral filtering: test distance against the local tangent plane equation $(p - p_{\text{center}}) \cdot N$.

### H-351. Noise Texture Bilinear Filtering Distorts Pseudo-Random Kernel Distribution
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAmbientOcclusionEffect.ts:140-165
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUAmbientOcclusionEffect.ts`, the 4x4 noise texture sampler is created with `minFilter: 'linear', magFilter: 'linear'`. Bilinear interpolation between adjacent noise texels averages random rotation vectors, reducing their variance and causing vector magnitude shrinkage.
* **Impact Analysis:** SSAO sample points clump together along diagonal axes, causing visible cross-hatching artifacts across flat surfaces.
* **Remediation Specification:** Configure the noise texture sampler with `minFilter: 'nearest', magFilter: 'nearest'`.

### H-352. Absence of Luminance Histogram: Linear Arithmetic Mean Subject to Outlier Clamping
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/AutoExposure.wgsl:38-70, 72-108
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `AutoExposure.wgsl`, average luminance is computed via linear arithmetic mean across downsampled tiles rather than a log-luminance histogram. A single bright light source or sun glint skews the arithmetic average.
* **Impact Analysis:** Looking toward the sun causes the entire landscape to plunge into pitch darkness, while small dark shadows cause severe overexposure.
* **Remediation Specification:** Implement a 256-bin log-luminance compute histogram with percentage-based low/high outlier clipping (e.g. 10th to 90th percentile).

### H-353. Fixed-Tick Temporal Smoothing Rate Lacking Frame Delta Time & Symmetric Adaptation
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAutoExposure.ts:165-185
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUAutoExposure.ts`, exposure smoothing multiplies by a fixed constant per frame ($0.05$) without accounting for variable frame delta time ($dt$), and uses identical rates for dark-to-bright and bright-to-dark adaptation.
* **Impact Analysis:** Exposure adaptation speed varies with framerate (2x faster at 120 FPS than 60 FPS), and violates human eye physiology (the human eye adapts to light in milliseconds but takes seconds to adapt to dark).
* **Remediation Specification:** Incorporate frame $dt$ into exponential decay: $1 - \exp(-dt / \tau)$, and provide asymmetric time constants for dark adaptation ($\tau \approx 1.5$s) vs light adaptation ($\tau \approx 0.3$s).

### H-354. Insufficient Dynamic Range Clamping (6.6 Stops) & Lack of APEX Calibration
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAutoExposure.ts:95-120
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUAutoExposure.ts`, exposure clamping bounds are hardcoded to $[0.1, 10.0]$, covering only 6.6 stops of dynamic range. Real-world planetary lighting spans from $10^{-4}$ lux (starlight) to $120,000$ lux (direct sun), requiring at least 25 stops of dynamic range.
* **Impact Analysis:** Sunlit daytime surfaces remain blown out and night scenes remain completely black, as auto-exposure hits hardclamp limits.
* **Remediation Specification:** Expand exposure clamping to $[10^{-5}, 10^5]$ and implement standard ISO 12232 APEX photometric calibration formulas.

### H-355. Asynchronous GPU-CPU-GPU Readback Round-Trip Delaying Adaptation by 1-2 Frames
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAutoExposure.ts:310-355
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUAutoExposure.ts`, calculated luminance is read back to CPU memory via `mapAsync`, checked in JavaScript, and uploaded back to the GPU uniform buffer, introducing 1-2 frames of latency and microtask queue contention.
* **Impact Analysis:** Stuttering exposure jumps and delayed compensation when transitioning between dark interiors and bright outdoors.
* **Remediation Specification:** Keep exposure calculation entirely GPU-resident: write exposure directly to a persistent GPU buffer bound to the tonemapping pass.

### H-356. Pre-Exposure Bloom Disconnect: Hardcoded SDR Bright-Pass Thresholding
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/BrightPass.wgsl:45-70
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `BrightPass.wgsl`, the bloom bright-pass threshold is specified as a static constant (e.g. 1.0) in un-exposed HDR radiance space, completely decoupled from dynamic scene auto-exposure.
* **Impact Analysis:** In dark night scenes, emissive objects fail to reach the static threshold and produce zero bloom; in bright day scenes, entire buildings exceed the threshold and bloom uncontrollably.
* **Remediation Specification:** Scale bright-pass thresholds by the current dynamic exposure value before luminance thresholding.

### H-357. HDR Framebuffer Format Incompatibility (rg11b10ufloat vs rgba16float) and Banding
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:450-485
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts`, intermediate HDR targets use `rg11b10ufloat`. This format lacks sign bits and allocates only 5 bits for blue channel precision.
* **Impact Analysis:** Severe color banding and green tinting in deep blue atmospheric night skies and twilight horizons.
* **Remediation Specification:** Standardize on `rgba16float` for all intermediate post-processing ping-pong render targets.

### H-358. Modified Reinhard Tonemapping Degeneracy Evaluating to Identity Pass Under Default WhitePoint
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/Tonemapping.wgsl:60-85
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `Tonemapping.wgsl`, modified Reinhard evaluates $C_{\text{out}} = \frac{C (1 + C / W^2)}{1 + C}$. When default `whitePoint` is set to $1.0$, the numerator simplifies to $C(1+C)$, causing the equation to evaluate identically to $C_{\text{out}} = C$.
* **Impact Analysis:** Tonemapping acts as a no-op identity pass, providing zero highlight compression and producing harsh 8-bit clipping at canvas blit.
* **Remediation Specification:** Set physical default whitePoint ($W \ge 5.0$) or replace Reinhard with standard ACES or Filmic tonemapping operators.

### H-359. Unclamped Triangular-PDF Dithering Generating Negative Floats in rgba16float
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/Tonemapping.wgsl:120-145
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `Tonemapping.wgsl`, triangular probability density function (TPDF) dither adds noise in range $[-1/255, +1/255]$ without clamping the result to non-negative values.
* **Impact Analysis:** Dark near-black pixels become negative floating-point values in `rgba16float`, producing NaNs in subsequent log-space color grading passes.
* **Remediation Specification:** Clamp final dithered color to `max(vec3<f32>(0.0), color)` before output.

### H-360. WebGL Reference Defect in AutoExposure.js Discarding 55.5% of Downsampling Samples
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Scene/AutoExposure.js:210-245
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `AutoExposure.js`, the WebGL downsampling pass hardcodes a 3x3 kernel with stride offsets that skip alternating pixels, evaluating only 4 out of 9 texels.
* **Impact Analysis:** Severe spatial aliasing in luminance metering; flashing bright lights between sample grid points causes exposure oscillation.
* **Remediation Specification:** Implement a continuous 13-tap bilateral downsampling filter that samples all source texels.

### H-361. ignJitter Collapses to a 1D Diagonal Ramp Lacking 2D Stratification
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUTAAEffect.ts:280-295, 785-806
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUTAAEffect.ts`, the Interleaved Gradient Noise (IGN) jitter sequence computes $x$ and $y$ offsets using identical phase multipliers, collapsing 2D sample distribution into a 1D diagonal line.
* **Impact Analysis:** Subpixel jitter fails to anti-alias horizontal and vertical edges, leaving staircase jaggies on buildings and coastlines.
* **Remediation Specification:** Implement standard Halton(2,3) 8-phase or 16-phase low-discrepancy sequence for subpixel camera jitter.

### H-362. Complete Omission of Variance Clipping & Naive Component-wise RGB Clamping
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/TAA.wgsl:115-133, 373-375
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `TAA.wgsl`, history color clamping uses component-wise min/max axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) clamping in RGB color space without statistical variance clipping (mean and variance in YCoCg).
* **Impact Analysis:** Moving objects leave severe ghosting trails, and clamped colors exhibit chromatic fringing and magenta/green color bleeding around moving edges.
* **Remediation Specification:** Transform color samples to YCoCg space, compute statistical mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$, and clip history against $[\mu - 1.25\sigma, \mu + 1.25\sigma]$.

### H-363. History Destruction and Frame Dropping on Resolution Change
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUTAAEffect.ts:410-445
* **Defect Mechanism:** When dynamic resolution scaling (DRS) or window resize changes framebuffer dimensions, `WebGPUTAAEffect.ts` immediately destroys the history texture and drops history blending for 2 frames.
* **Impact Analysis:** Dynamic resolution scaling triggers visible full-screen flashing and edge crawling on every resolution step change.
* **Remediation Specification:** Retain history textures during DRS adjustments, resampling history UVs by `previousResolution / currentResolution`.

### H-364. Absence of Karis Anti-Firefly Filtering and Multi-Scale Pyramid Blur in Bloom
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUBloomEffect.ts:265-295
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUBloomEffect.ts`, bloom blur applies a single-stage wide Gaussian blur rather than a progressive multi-scale down/up pyramid (Karis filter).
* **Impact Analysis:** Subpixel specular highlights generate severe temporal flickering "fireflies", and bloom glow has an unnatural uniform Gaussian halo rather than wide atmospheric light bleed.
* **Remediation Specification:** Implement a 5-stage progressive dual-filtering downsample/upsample blur pyramid with Karis weighting ($1 / (1 + L)$) on downsampling.

### H-365. Depth of Field Near-Field Bleed and Lack of Bokeh Morphology
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/DepthOfField.wgsl:58-73
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `DepthOfField.wgsl`, foreground blur gathers background sharp pixels indiscriminately because blur weighting does not account for near-field circle of confusion occluding background geometry.
* **Impact Analysis:** In-focus background objects bleed into blurry foreground silhouettes, creating unnatural dark outlines and ghosted edges.
* **Remediation Specification:** Separate DoF into near-field and far-field accumulation buffers, weighting near-field gather by foreground CoC.

### H-366. Unpooled VRAM Allocation Thrashing and Texture Destruction on Viewport Resize
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUBloomEffect.ts:145-180
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUBloomEffect.ts`, intermediate mip textures are created with exact viewport dimensions and destroyed on every resize event.
* **Impact Analysis:** Dragging a browser window edge creates dozens of un-pooled GPU textures per second, triggering WebGPU memory exhaustion crashes.
* **Remediation Specification:** Allocate textures using power-of-two pooled buckets and bind dynamic sub-rect viewports.

### H-367. Discontinuous 333 km Orbital Space Pop and Spurious Low Earth Orbit Sky Glow
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/SkyAtmosphere.wgsl:855-880
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `SkyAtmosphere.wgsl`, the shader abruptly switches between sky-view LUT sampling and space rendering at altitude $h = 333$ km without alpha blending.
* **Impact Analysis:** Zooming from Low Earth Orbit into the atmosphere produces a jarring one-frame pop where space turns from black to bright cyan.
* **Remediation Specification:** Implement smooth hermite cubic interpolation over a transition band ($h \in [300, 350]$ km).

### H-368. Missing Lunar Opposition Surge Coupling in Atmospheric Scattering and Moonglow
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/SkyAtmosphereCommon.glsl:85-115
* **Defect Mechanism:** Atmospheric light scattering evaluates only the primary sun directional vector, completely omitting secondary illumination from the Moon and lunar opposition surge.
* **Impact Analysis:** Nighttime skies illuminated by a full moon render completely pitch black, lacking realistic moonglow and night atmospheric radiance.
* **Remediation Specification:** Add a secondary light source evaluation in atmosphere LUT computation scaled by lunar phase irradiance.

### H-369. 48-Arcminute Sun Deadband and Scene-Light Decoupling in LUT Bake
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAtmosphereLUT.ts:180-210
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUAtmosphereLUT.ts`, atmosphere LUTs are re-baked only when the sun angle changes by more than 48 arcminutes ($0.8^\circ$), while scene lighting updates continuously every frame.
* **Impact Analysis:** Shadows and terrain lighting move smoothly, but atmospheric sky color jumps in visible discrete steps every few minutes during sunset.
* **Remediation Specification:** Decouple fast runtime phase function evaluation from slow precomputed transmittance LUTs, or interpolate between dual time-sliced LUT bakes.

### H-370. Oblate Ellipsoid Radius Discrepancy Between LUT Bake and Uniform Buffer
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAtmosphereUniforms.ts:90-125
* **Defect Mechanism:** Atmosphere LUT precomputation assumes a spherical planet with radius $R = 6,371,000$m, while Cesium WGS84 ellipsoid uniforms use semi-major axis $a = 6,378,137$m and semi-minor axis $b = 6,356,752$m.
* **Impact Analysis:** At polar regions, the atmosphere floats 15 km above the ice caps, while at the equator, mountains protrude unnaturally through atmospheric layers.
* **Remediation Specification:** Compute local ellipsoid curvature radius at the camera nadir point and pass dynamic curvature radius into atmosphere uniform buffers.

### H-371. 32-bit Uint32Array Counter Overflow and 24-Bit Hash Collision at 4,096 Features
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/GraphicsContext.ts:1649-1665, packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/FeatureIdResolve.wgsl:15-40
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `GraphicsContext.ts`, pick IDs are generated by a monotonically increasing 32-bit counter, but `FeatureIdResolve.js` truncates the ID to a 24-bit hash in `FeatureIdResolve.wgsl`. By birthday paradox, hash collisions occur with $> 50$% probability at just 4,096 distinct features.
* **Impact Analysis:** In dense 3D Tilesets (e.g. New York or Tokyo city models), clicking on one building selects a completely different building miles away.
* **Remediation Specification:** Implement a generational slot allocator with dense index recycling, and preserve 32-bit integer IDs in pick textures (`r32uint`).

### H-372. Query Rectangle Width/Height Unscaled by Device Pixel Ratio on High-DPI Displays
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Scene/Picking.js:1522-1534, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts:893-896
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `Picking.js`, picking search rectangles compute pixel bounds in CSS pixels (e.g. 3x3 window) without scaling by `window.devicePixelRatio`. On Retina / 4K displays with DPR 2.0 or 3.0, the scissor box evaluates to less than 1 physical device pixel.
* **Impact Analysis:** Clicking on thin polylines, points, or billboard icons on high-DPI monitors and mobile devices misses the target almost every time.
* **Remediation Specification:** Multiply picking query rectangle dimensions by `devicePixelRatio` when computing the scissor rect in `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts`.

### H-373. Pseudo-Pool GPUBuffer Churn and In-Flight Drop on Rapid Hover Picking
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPickTransientReadback.ts:45-93, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts:1379, 1705
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `WebGPUPickTransientReadback.ts`, mouse move hover events allocate a new staging `GPUBuffer` on every move event. If the user moves the mouse rapidly, in-flight staging buffers are overwritten or dropped, and standalone `queue.submit` calls flood the GPU command queue.
* **Impact Analysis:** High-frequency mouse movement causes micro-freezes, GC spikes, and dropped tooltips.
* **Remediation Specification:** Implement a ring buffer pool of pre-allocated staging buffers and throttle hover pick dispatches to display refresh rate.

## Part 39: Wave 13 Architectural Modernization & Performance Vectors (P2)

### M-190. Canvas Pass Redirection of Deferred Splats in OIT
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.ts:310-325
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Gaussian splat rendering defers sorting and accumulation to specialized compute passes, but `WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.ts` attempts to redirect splats through standard OIT accumulation shaders.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Decouple splat rasterization into a dedicated radix-sorted tile splat pass executed prior to composite.

### M-191. Absence of Stochastic Transparency / Alpha-to-Coverage Fallback for Dense Particle Fields
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:500-530
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Rendering millions of translucent particles (smoke, rain, dust) through multi-pass OIT causes severe accumulation buffer fill-rate saturation.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Provide alpha-to-coverage and stochastic screen-door transparency fallback paths for dense particle systems.

### M-192. Percentage-Closer Soft Shadows (PCSS) Missing Blocker Search Architecture
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Model/ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:1645-1665, packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Shadow/ShadowReceiveCSM.wgsl:115-130
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Cesium shadows only implement static 3x3 Percentage-Closer Filtering (PCF). Lack of non-comparison shadow samplers prevents implementing variable penumbra PCSS blocker search.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Expose non-comparison texture view bindings for shadow depth textures and implement PCSS blocker search with contact hardening.

### M-193. Contact Shadows Screen-Edge Popping Due to Abrupt Viewport Exit
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/ContactShadows.wgsl:155-159
* **Architectural Mechanism:** When screen-space shadow raymarching steps cross outside the viewport bounds, the shader breaks immediately without evaluating distance-to-edge attenuation.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Apply smooth Hermite boundary attenuation ($	ext{smoothstep}(0.0, 0.1, 	ext{uv})$) to fade out contact shadows near screen edges.

### M-194. Models and 3D Tiles Omit Cloud Shadow Sampling
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Model/ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:3179-3204
* **Architectural Mechanism:** `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` contains no cloud shadow texture bindings or attenuation math. While terrain is darkened by clouds, 3D buildings remain lit at 100% sunlight.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Inject cloud shadow texture sampling and attenuation factors into `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` fragment evaluation.

### M-195. Per-Frame GPUBindGroup Re-Allocation in AO Post-Process Pipeline
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAmbientOcclusionEffect.ts:340-375
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Bind groups for ambient occlusion generation and modulation passes are created new on every frame invocation.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Cache bind groups keyed by input texture resource IDs and uniform buffer revisions.

### M-196. Static Kernel Array Bound in Uniform Buffer Rather Than Workgroup Shared Memory
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/AmbientOcclusionGenerate.wgsl:30-45
* **Architectural Mechanism:** The 32-sample SSAO kernel vector array is loaded from a dynamic uniform buffer on every thread sample instruction.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Store sample kernel vectors in `workgroup` shared memory or WGSL private const array to eliminate UBO cache pressure.

### M-197. Lack of Temporal Reprojection Filter (TAO) for Ambient Occlusion
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAmbientOcclusionEffect.ts:410-440
* **Architectural Mechanism:** AO samples are evaluated purely per-frame without temporal history accumulation, requiring high sample counts (32-64 samples) to suppress noise.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Implement a Temporal Ambient Occlusion (TAO) filter using motion vectors and history reprojection to achieve clean results at 4-8 samples/pixel.

### M-198. Horizon Cosine-Weighted Sampling Missing in Screen-Space Directional Occlusion
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/AmbientOcclusionGenerate.wgsl:229-255
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Screen-space directional occlusion samples space uniformly across azimuth rather than weighting by cosine of elevation angle relative to surface normal.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Incorporate cosine-weighted hemisphere distribution into GTAO/SSDO horizon integration.

### M-199. Static Workgroup Tile Sizing Causing GPU Thread Divergence on Silhouettes
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/AmbientOcclusionGenerate.wgsl:10-25
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Compute workgroups use static 16x16 thread layout. On complex geometric boundaries, branch divergence between foreground objects and background sky degrades compute efficiency.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Optimize workgroup dispatch layout to 8x8 with early workgroup-level depth range pre-classification.

### M-200. 256-Bin Logarithmic Compute Histogram with Subgroup Operations
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/AutoExposure.wgsl:74-110
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Workgroup reductions currently rely on atomicAdd memory serialization in shared workgroup memory.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Modernize luminance histogram compute shader using WebGPU subgroup ballot and arithmetic operations (`subgroupAdd`).

### M-201. Direct GPU-Resident Exposure Buffer Eliminating CPU Readback Roundtrip
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAutoExposure.ts:410-445
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Exposure values are read back to CPU memory and rewritten to GPU uniforms every frame.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Maintain persistent GPU-resident exposure uniform buffer with direct compute-to-raster bind group linkage.

### M-202. Multi-Pass Compute Dispatch Sizing Modernization for Arbitrary Resolutions
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAutoExposure.ts:280-305
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Compute pass dispatch sizes assume fixed power-of-two dimensions, causing edge thread underflow on arbitrary window sizes.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Calculate dynamic grid dispatch dimensions via `Math.ceil(width / workgroupSizeX)` with bounds checking.

### M-203. Exposure-Aware Atmospheric Glare, SunHalo & Vignette Modernization
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:1820-1865
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Atmospheric optical effects (sun glare, halo, vignette) calculate intensities independently of auto-exposure.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Pass dynamic exposure scale uniforms to optical shader stages to ensure photometric coherence across exposure adjustments.

### M-204. Hardcoded Blend Weight Without Velocity or Disocclusion Adaptation
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/TAA.wgsl:376-381
* **Architectural Mechanism:** In `TAA.wgsl`, temporal feedback blend weight is hardcoded to $0.90$ across all pixels, regardless of whether a pixel is stationary, moving rapidly, or newly disoccluded.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Adapt blend weight dynamically based on motion vector magnitude, local depth gradients, and color variance.

### M-205. Incoherent Occlusion Hierarchy Between SunBloom and SunHalo
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSunBloomEffect.ts:90-125
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Sun bloom and sun halo effects execute in separate post-processing passes with differing occlusion test parameters, causing sun flares to persist after the sun disc disappears.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Unify solar optical passes under a single coherent solar visibility evaluator that shares depth occlusion factors.

### M-206. Float16 Precision Limits and Linear Zenith Horizon Smearing in LUTs
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/AtmosphereLUT.wgsl:80-115
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Atmosphere LUTs use linear altitude and zenith angle parameterization with half-precision float (`rgba16float`), losing resolution near the grazing horizon.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Implement non-linear spherical coordinate parameterization ($u = \sqrt{h / H}$) and upgrade sky-view LUTs to `rgba32float`.

### M-207. Single-Precision Catastrophic Cancellation in World-Coordinate Ray-Sphere Intersection
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/SkyAtmosphereCommon.glsl:49-65
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Ray-sphere intersection formulas evaluate $b^2 - 4ac$ using single-precision floats with coordinates exceeding $6.378 \times 10^6$m, causing discriminant cancellation.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Normalize ray origins to camera-relative local height and evaluate ray intersections in dimensionless units.

### M-208. Ozone Layer Quadrature Aliasing Under Adaptive Low Step Counts
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/AtmosphereLUT.wgsl:410-445
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Ozone absorption peaks sharply at 25 km altitude with narrow thickness (Chappuis band). Under coarse numerical integration (16-32 steps), rays skip the ozone layer entirely at low sun angles.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Implement adaptive Simpson quadrature rule or importance-sampled integration concentrated at the stratospheric ozone layer.

### M-209. Multiple Scattering Approximation Lacks Spherical Directional Integration
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/AtmosphereLUT.wgsl:520-565
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Multiple scattering computation approximates higher-order scattering via an isotropic scalar factor rather than integrating full spherical directional radiance.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Implement precomputed dual-scattering LUT (Hillaire 2020) integrating 2nd-order scattered directional flux.

### M-210. Inter-Slice Depth Clear Resets Depth to 1.0 Between Frustum Passes
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts:609-612
* **Architectural Mechanism:** In multi-frustum picking passes, the depth attachment is cleared to 1.0 at the beginning of each frustum slice pass, allowing near-slice objects to overwrite far-slice objects without depth bounds checking.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Track per-slice depth bounds and preserve nearest picked ID across all frustum slices.

## Part 40: Wave 14 Critical Core Vulnerabilities (P0)

### C-288. WebGPU CommandEncoder Invalidation & Device Loss via Unwritten Query Range Resolution
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUTimestampProfiler.ts:432-454, 503-510, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPerformanceManager.ts:657-670, packages/engine/Source/Scene/Scene.js:6505-6670
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** `WebGPUPerformanceManager.withRenderPassTimestamps(descriptor)` eagerly reserves query slot pairs (`beginIndex`, `endIndex`) and records pass records before the pass encoder begins. In `WebGPUTimestampProfiler.endFrame()`, `encoder.resolveQuerySet(querySet, 0, queryCount, resolveBuffer, 0)` is invoked across the full range `[0, queryCount)`. Under WebGPU Spec §18.3, every query in the resolved range must have been written by an active pass. When dynamic passes (e.g. shadow cascade, picking, or post-processing) abort or throw before recording, unwritten query slots remain in the range, triggering a fatal Dawn validation error: `Query [X] in [QuerySet] has not been written`. This invalidates the `GPUCommandEncoder`, causing `queue.submit()` rejection and immediate GPU device loss.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** A dynamic render pass aborts due to culling or a 0x0 canvas. Resolving unwritten query indices invalidates the frame encoder, crashing the WebGPU device and terminating the render loop.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Decouple query index reservation from descriptor setup by assigning indices only within active pass encoders, or record a committed query bitmap and emit non-contiguous `resolveQuerySet` ranges covering only written queries.

### C-289. Permanent Slot Deadlock and Ring Starvation on Unsubmitted Frames
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUContext.ts:3388-3411, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUTimestampProfiler.ts:411-417, 518-522, 542-555
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `WebGPUPerformanceManager.endFrame()`, `profiler.endFrame(encoder)` marks `state.readbackPending = true` and queues the frame slot into `_pendingSubmissions`. `afterSubmit()` is only reached after `_submitPendingTextureMipJobs()`, `finish()`, and `queue.submit()`. If an exception escapes during mip jobs or submit, `afterSubmit()` is skipped. The slot remains permanently flagged with `readbackPending: true`. Over subsequent cycles, all ring slots are permanently starved, locking the profiler into 100% skipped readbacks forever.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** A transient error during texture mip generation aborts frame submission. All 3 profiler ring buffer slots become permanently deadlocked, disabling GPU timing telemetry for the remainder of the session.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Wrap queue submit in `WebGPUContext.ts` in `try...finally` to invoke `profiler.abortPendingSubmissions()`, resetting `readbackPending = false` on unsubmitted slots and logging a lost sample count.

### C-290. Vertical Y-Axis Inversion / Upside-Down Cluster Mapping in Fragment Lighting
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/ClusterBounds.wgsl:127-128, packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/chunks/structs/ClusteredLighting.wgsl:130-131, packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/ClusterDebugVisualize.wgsl:76-77
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `ClusterBounds.wgsl`, cluster AABBs are generated in NDC where `y = -1.0` is the bottom of the frustum (`yMinNdc = -1.0 + gid.y * tileSizeY`), making `gid.y = 0` the bottom row. In contrast, fragment shaders (`ClusteredLighting.wgsl` and `ClusterDebugVisualize.wgsl`) derive `tileY` from `@builtin(position)` where `y = 0.0` is the top-left of the framebuffer (`tileY = floor(fragCoord.y / tileSizeY)`). Consequently, fragments in the top half of the screen sample light clusters from the bottom half, and vice versa.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Punctual lights placed at the top of the view frustum (e.g. streetlights or ceiling fixtures) illuminate terrain and objects at the bottom of the viewport, while lights at the bottom illuminate the sky, creating inverted lighting across all clustered PBR models.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Invert NDC Y in `ClusterBounds.wgsl` (`yMaxNdc = 1.0 - gid.y * tileSizeY; yMinNdc = yMaxNdc - tileSizeY`) or invert `tileY` in `ClusteredLighting.wgsl` (`tileY = (CL_TILE_COUNT_Y - 1u) - u32(...)`).

### C-291. Division-by-Zero and NaN Poisoning on Zero `inverseProjection` in 2D/Ortho
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/ClusterBounds.wgsl:76-80, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRendererClusteredLighting.ts:320, 349, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/UniformStateComputations.js:280-290
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `UniformStateComputations.js`, `inverseProjection` is populated with `Matrix4.ZERO` when in 2D mode, morphing, or orthographic 3D mode. In `ClusterBounds.wgsl`, `unprojectNdcToView` multiplies NDC by `inverseProjection` and divides by `view.w`. When `view.w = 0.0`, IEEE-754 produces `0.0 / 0.0 = NaN`. All 3,456 cluster bounding boxes are populated with `NaN`, causing all light intersection tests in `ClusterAssign.wgsl` to fail.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Switching the viewer to 2D mode, Columbus View, or engaging an orthographic camera while clustered lighting is active immediately poisons cluster bounding boxes with NaNs, causing all punctual lights to extinguish.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Add a singular/zero matrix check in `WebGPUSceneRendererClusteredLighting.ts` to bypass cluster generation in 2D/ortho, and guard `unprojectNdcToView` in WGSL against zero `view.w`.

### C-292. Constant 0 Availability Inversion Corrupts `availableCount` and Metadata Table Sizing
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Scene/ImplicitAvailabilityBitstream.js:31-37, packages/engine/Source/Scene/ImplicitSubtree.js:478-480, 935-941, 1032-1054
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `ImplicitAvailabilityBitstream.js`, `if (defined(constant))` sets `availableCount = lengthBits` under the assumption that `constant` can only ever be 1 (`true`). However, 3D Tiles 1.1 defines `constant: 0` (`false`) for unavailable layers. Because `defined(false)` is `true`, `availableCount` is inverted to `lengthBits` (100% available).
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Sparse 3D Tilesets or subtrees with `constant: 0` content availability report full availability. Metadata parsers attempt to construct `MetadataTable` instances with `count = lengthBits`, throwing buffer underflow `RangeError`s and corrupting memory.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Update `ImplicitAvailabilityBitstream.js` to assign `availableCount = constant ? lengthBits : 0`.

### C-293. Unbounded RAM Leak — Decoded Implicit Subtrees Are Excluded from LRU Eviction
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Scene/Cesium3DTile.js:717-720, 1131-1140, 1956-1962, packages/engine/Source/Scene/Cesium3DTileset.js:3183-3190, 3773-3789, packages/engine/Source/Scene/Implicit3DTileContent.js:260-291, 580
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** Tiles with implicit content are explicitly excluded from `tileset._cache` (`!this.hasImplicitContent`). Placeholder tiles have `hasRenderableContent = false`, causing `unloadContent()` to return immediately. Subtree topology, jump buffers, and metadata tables are only destroyed on HTTP expiration, never by LRU eviction. Transcoded tiles retain strong references to `implicitSubtree`.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Roaming across a Google Photorealistic 3D Tileset or large implicit 3D city causes decoded subtrees, availability buffers, and tile hierarchies to accumulate monotonically in the JavaScript heap, leaking hundreds of megabytes until the browser tab crashes with an OOM.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Enforce LRU tracking on implicit subtrees in `Cesium3DTilesetCache`, trigger `destroySubtree()` when memory budgets are exceeded, and replace circular tile-subtree references with `WeakRef` handles.

### C-294. Traversal Black Hole & Permanent LOD Freeze on Child Subtree Network / 404 Failure
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Scene/Cesium3DTile.js:1413-1418, 1457-1459, 1808-1810, 1853-1855, packages/engine/Source/Scene/Cesium3DTilesetBaseTraversal.js:106-147, 208-232, packages/engine/Source/Scene/Cesium3DTilesetTraversal.js:58-68, 131-138
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** When a child `.subtree` request fails (HTTP 404, CORS, or timeout), `tile._contentState` transitions to `FAILED`. In `Cesium3DTilesetBaseTraversal`, refinement requires all children to be available (`refines = refines && child.contentAvailable`). Because the failed child never becomes available, parent refinement is permanently blocked. For empty placeholder parents, neither parent nor child is selected for rendering.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** A single missing or 404 child subtree file freezes refinement across its entire hierarchy. Under `REPLACE` refinement, low-LOD parent geometry remains stuck at point-blank range; under empty parent nodes, the geometry vanishes entirely, creating an invisible black hole in the world.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Handle `child.contentFailed` in traversal by treating failed subtrees as terminal leaf boundaries or falling back to available sibling tiles, avoiding infinite refinement blocks.

### C-295. WGSL Struct Member Padding Violation & UBO Layout Misalignment in Custom Shaders
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Scene/Model/CustomShaderWGSLPipelineStage.js:108, 212-227, 371-394, 456-463, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:3561-3573
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `emitUniformStruct`, a `_czm_pad: vec4<f32>` (16-byte alignment) is appended after single-slot uniforms (`f32`, `vec2`, `vec3`), causing WGSL to insert 12 bytes of padding and allocating 32 bytes per scalar. In contrast, CPU packing assumes a 16-byte slot stride. Furthermore, `mat2x2<f32>` (which requires 16 bytes in WGSL) is allocated 32 bytes on the CPU with misaligned column strides.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Any CustomShader declaring multiple scalar/vector uniforms either reads zero/garbage data on the GPU due to offset desynchronization or fails WebGPU pipeline validation with "Binding size is smaller than the minimum buffer binding size".
* **Architectural Remediation:** Replace `vec4<f32>` padding with exact type-specific scalar padding (`vec3<f32>` for `f32`, `vec2<f32>` for `vec2`, `f32` for `vec3`), and correct `mat2` to 16 bytes with 8-byte column alignment.

### C-296. Complete No-Op / Discarded Vertex Custom Shader Output in Model WGSL
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Model/ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:1119-1138, packages/engine/Source/Scene/Model/CustomShaderWGSLPipelineStage.js:334-343
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl`, `czm_customVertexMain(csVsInput, &csVsOutput)` is invoked on a stack-allocated `csVsOutput` struct at the very end of `vertexMain`. The mutated `csVsOutput.positionMC` is immediately discarded when the block exits; `output.position`, `output.positionEC`, and `output.rteMC` are never updated. Furthermore, clip projection and log depth have already executed prior to this block.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Custom vertex shaders written in WGSL (vertex displacement, terrain deformation, flag waving, procedural mesh offsets) are 100% silent no-ops. Geometry renders completely unperturbed.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Relocate the custom vertex hook to the beginning of `vertexMain` before RTE and clip projection, read back `csVsOutput.positionMC`, and recompute `positionEC`, `rteMC`, `output.position`, and `output.v_logDepth`.

### C-297. Broken Primitive Cache Invalidation on CustomShader Mutation Causing Stale Pipelines & Destroyed Buffer Crash
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:3508-3511, 3536-3538, 3562-3564, 3693-3695, 4117, 4932-4942, 6646-6665, 6837-6850

When `model.customShader` is changed or set to undefined, `uboBuffer` is destroyed, but cached `textureEntries` retain references to the destroyed buffer. On subsequent frames, cached bind groups reuse the destroyed buffer handle.

* **Architectural Remediation:** Track `_customShaderClassHash` on `PrimitiveRenderData`, include custom shader hash checks in primitive cache invalidation predicates, and rebuild texture/UBO bind groups whenever `uboBuffer` is recreated.

### C-298. Quadtree Traversal Uncaught TypeError Crash at Level 31
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Scene/QuadtreePrimitive.js:584-586, 825-826
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** `QuadtreePrimitive.js` statically allocates `traversalQuadsByLevel = new Array(31)` (indices 0..30). When a tile refines at level 30, its children are constructed at `level = 31`. In `visitVisibleChildrenNearToFar`, evaluating `traversalQuadsByLevel[31]` yields `undefined`, throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'southwest')`.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Zooming in closely on sub-centimeter photogrammetry, high-density drone scans, or high-zoom 2D map views triggers level 31 refinement, instantly crashing the animation loop with an uncaught exception.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Dynamically expand `traversalQuadsByLevel` or enforce an engine-wide `QuadtreePrimitive.MAX_LEVEL = 30` safeguard in `canRefine(tile)`.

### C-299. Antimeridian Longitude Calculation Breakdown & Tile Range Corruption
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Core/GeographicTilingScheme.js:151-174, 201-208
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `GeographicTilingScheme.prototype.positionToTileXY`, when a rectangle crosses the antimeridian (`rectangle.east < rectangle.west`), `longitude += TWO_PI` is applied unconditionally to all coordinates, including positive ones ($170^\circ \le \lambda \le 180^\circ$), mapping them to $532^\circ$ and clamping them to `xTiles - 1`. In `tileXYToRectangle`, radians are not normalized, producing un-normalized extents ($185^\circ$ to $190^\circ$) that fail `Rectangle.contains()`.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Imagery and terrain layers covering antimeridian regions (Fiji, Aleutian Islands, New Zealand) map points to the wrong tiles and fail height/picking queries.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Only add `TWO_PI` when `longitude < rectangle.west`, and normalize output tile bounds via `CesiumMath.negativePiToPi()`.

### C-300. Unhandled TypeError on Out-of-Bounds / Polar Web Mercator Tile Requests
* **Target Subsystems:** packages/engine/Source/Scene/ImageryLayerHelpers.js:163-178, packages/engine/Source/Core/WebMercatorTilingScheme.js:251-256
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** When querying tiles near or beyond Web Mercator projection bounds ($\pm 85.0511287798^\circ$), `WebMercatorTilingScheme.prototype.positionToTileXY` returns `undefined`. `ImageryLayerHelpers.js` fails to check for `undefined` and accesses `northwestTileCoordinates.x`, throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'x')`.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Viewing northern Greenland, Svalbard, or Antarctica with standard Web Mercator base imagery (Bing, OSM, Google) crashes terrain imagery texture updates.
