### H-476. Universal Arena Slot Leak Across Engine Lifecycle & Defective `destroy()` Implementations
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Scene/WasmArenaSlots.js:87-107`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/WasmSortBridge.js:307-313`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/WasmHeightmapBridge.js:253-259`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/WasmQuantizedMeshBridge.js:218-224`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/WasmRTEBridge.js:420-426`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/WasmMatrixBridge.js:299-305`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/WasmPointCloudBridge.js:544-550`, - `packages/engine/Source/Core/WasmFeatureDetection.js:173-181`, - `packages/wasm/src/lib.rs:88-110, 153-160, 171-174`
* **Defect Mechanism:** `ARENAS` consists of 8 static `Mutex<Vec<u8>>` slots. `WasmArenaSlots.js` defines slot IDs 0 through 7.
  However, six out of the seven bridges (`Sort`, `Heightmap`, `QuantizedMesh`, `RTE`, `Matrix`, `PointCloud`) fail to import or call `freeSlot(wasmModule, slot)`.
  In their `destroy()` methods, all six invoke `WasmFeatureDetection.freeBuffer(_wasmModule)`.
  In `packages/wasm/src/lib.rs:171-174`:
  ```rust
  pub fn free_buffer() {
      free_buffer_slot(DEFAULT_SLOT);
  }
  ```
  `free_buffer()` forwards exclusively to `DEFAULT_SLOT` (slot 0)!
  Slots 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 are NEVER freed!
  Only `WasmCullBridge.js:335` calls `freeSlot(_wasmModule, WasmArenaSlot.CULL)`.
  Furthermore, `WasmCullBridge.js:250` claims in JSDoc to use `try/finally` to free buffers per operation, but contains NO `finally` block and never frees per-operation.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** During prolonged browsing sessions where terrain tiles, point clouds, and models are loaded and unloaded, memory allocated in WASM linear memory for slots 2 through 7 (tens of megabytes per slot) is permanently retained in static memory. Destroying the Viewer or cleaning up scenes fails to release this memory, causing monotonic memory leaks and browser crashes on memory-constrained devices.
* **Architectural Remediation:** 1. Update `destroy()` across all bridges to import and call `freeSlot(_wasmModule, this._arenaSlot)`.
  2. Implement an engine-wide `free_all_slots()` export in Rust to reset all arenas upon Viewer teardown.

### H-486. Ephemeral Heap Allocations & BigInt Overhead in Protobuf Decoding
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Scene/decodeMVT.js:308-322, 333-353, 363-392`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/decodeMVT.js:475-484`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/decodeMVT.js:512-538`
* **Defect Mechanism:** 1. In `decodeMVT.js:512-538`, `readBigVarint` creates `0n` and performs 64-bit BigInt bitwise operations (`BigInt(byte & 0x7f) << shift;`) for every single varint in the tile. `readVarint32` (lines 475-484) wraps each varint into a newly instantiated heap object `{ value: Number(value.value), newPos: value.newPos }`.
  2. In `decodeGeometry` (lines 308-392), points are decoded as distinct object allocations: `points.push({ x, y })`, `current.push({ x, y })`.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** A standard production vector tile (e.g. OpenMapTiles, Mapbox Streets) contains 50,000 to 200,000 vertices and hundreds of thousands of tag indices. `decodeMVT` allocates over 1,500,000 short-lived JavaScript objects and BigInt primitives per tile. Under multi-tile streaming during fast camera pans, V8 enters Major GC thrashing cycles, dropping frame rates from 60 fps to single digits.
* **Architectural Remediation:** 1. Replace `readBigVarint` for 32-bit fields with a zero-allocation integer varint reader that writes into a reusable scratch object or returns packed values directly.
  2. Decode geometry directly into contiguous typed arrays (`Int32Array` or `Float32Array`) rather than arrays of `{ x, y }` objects.

### H-487. Main-Thread Structured Cloning & Missing ArrayBuffer Transfer in MVTTileDecoder
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Scene/MVTTileDecoder.js:60-67`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/MVTDataProvider.js:49-54`
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `MVTTileDecoder.js:60-67`:
  ```js
  MVTTileDecoder.decode = function (parameters) {
    const taskProcessor = MVTTileDecoder._getTaskProcessor();
    // Deliberately do NOT transfer parameters.arrayBuffer: keeping the buffer
    // intact on the main thread preserves the synchronous fallback...
    return taskProcessor.scheduleTask(parameters);
  };
  ```
  Because `parameters.arrayBuffer` is omitted from `transferableObjects`, the browser performs a synchronous deep structured clone of the binary buffer on the main thread. Furthermore, in `MVTDataProvider.js:52-54`, `decodeInWorker` defaults to `false`, causing all vector tiles to decode synchronously on the main rendering thread unless explicitly overridden.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Loading high-density MVT tiles (often 5 MB to 20 MB compressed/uncompressed) forces multi-megabyte buffer copies on the main thread for every tile. When combined with default synchronous decoding, panning across dense urban regions freezes the animation loop for 80–250 ms per tile.
* **Architectural Remediation:** 1. Make worker decoding opt-out rather than default-off in `MVTDataProvider.js`.
  2. Transfer `parameters.arrayBuffer` to the worker. If fallback is needed on worker failure, retain a lightweight network retry or clone only on explicit failure.

### H-488. Full-Buffer Uploads on Dirty Range Mutations in WebGPUBufferPrimitiveRenderers
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUBufferPolygonRenderer.ts:458-472`, - `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUBufferPolylineRenderer.ts:593-627`
* **Defect Mechanism:** While `WebGPUBufferPolygonRenderer.ts` lines 16-17 advertise that *"A dirty range is repacked on the CPU and uploaded through `writeBuffer` without a full reupload"*, the actual implementation in lines 458-472 unconditionally uploads the full allocated buffers:
  ```ts
  function uploadPolygonBuffers(device: GPUDevice, cache: PolygonCache): void {
    device.queue.writeBuffer(cache.positionHigh, 0, gpuData(cache.positionHighArr));
    device.queue.writeBuffer(cache.positionLow, 0, gpuData(cache.positionLowArr));
    device.queue.writeBuffer(cache.pickColor, 0, gpuData(cache.pickColorArr));
    device.queue.writeBuffer(cache.showAndColor, 0, gpuData(cache.showAndColorArr));
    device.queue.writeBuffer(cache.indexBuffer, 0, gpuData(cache.indexArr));
  }
  ```
  `WebGPUBufferPolylineRenderer.ts:593-627` exhibits identical behavior across 8 buffers.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** In a dynamic vector collection with `vertexCountMax = 500,000`, updating or adding a single polygon dirty element triggers a full re-upload of over 35 MB of vertex and index data across the PCIe bus on that frame.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Calculate exact dirty byte offsets and byte lengths from `collection._dirtyOffset` and `collection._dirtyCount` and pass the subarray views to `device.queue.writeBuffer(buffer, bufferOffset, data, dataOffset, size)`.

### H-489. Brittle URL Coordinate Parsing & Global Origin Fallback in MVTDataProvider
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Scene/MVTDataProvider.js:222-236`
* **Defect Mechanism:** `parseTileCoordinates` relies on a rigid regular expression:
  ```js
  const match = url.match(/\/(\d+)\/(\d+)\/(\d+)(?:\.[^/?#]+)?(?:[?#]|$)/i);
  if (!match) {
    // Falls back to z/x/y = 0/0/0
    return { tileZ: 0, tileX: 0, tileY: 0 };
  }
  return {
    tileZ: parseInt(match[1], 10),
    tileX: parseInt(match[2], 10),
    tileY: parseInt(match[3], 10),
  };
  ```
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** 1. Proxy or custom endpoints with numbered path prefixes (e.g. `/v1/service/3857/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf`) capture the prefix numbers (`3857`, `z`, `x`), completely scrambling tile coordinates.
  2. Query-parameter templated URLs (e.g. `tile?z={z}&x={x}&y={y}`) fail the regex match completely, causing all requested tiles to fall back to `{ tileZ: 0, tileX: 0, tileY: 0 }`. Hundreds of tiles are incorrectly positioned at the null island root tile.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Pass `tile.x`, `tile.y`, and `tile.level` directly from the `Cesium3DTile` object through `createContent(tileset, tile, resource, arrayBuffer)` instead of attempting to reverse-engineer coordinates from the URL string.

### H-490. Dangling Destroyed GPUTexture References in Bind Group Caches during Perlin-Worley Upgrade
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUProceduralCloudRenderer.ts:2938-2949`, - `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUProceduralCloudRenderer.ts:1464-1484`
* **Defect Mechanism:** When `needPW` evaluates to true in `ensureNoiseBaked` (line 2938), `cache.noise.shapeTexture.destroy()` and `cache.noise.detailTexture.destroy()` are called to rebuild resources with the PW variant. However, `clearCloudCompositeBindGroupCaches(cache, lease)` is never called. `cache.mainBindGroups` (lines 1464-1484) continues to retain entries storing `entry.shapeView`, `entry.detailView`, and `entry.bindGroup` created from the destroyed textures.

Upon command buffer submission, WebGPU validation fails with `[Invalid Texture] is used in [BindGroup]`, aborting the render pass and blacking out the frame.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Whenever `needPW` executes in `ensureNoiseBaked`, invoke `clearCloudCompositeBindGroupCaches(cache, lease)` and invalidate `cache.shadowBindGroups`.

### H-491. Non-Directional "Silver Lining" Rim Light Glow in Anti-Sun Backscatter and Night
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/ProceduralClouds.wgsl:2716-2721`
* **Defect Mechanism:** Line 2717 computes `silverLining = cloud.silverLiningIntensity * pow(clamp(1.0 - density * 3.0, 0.0, 1.0), 2.0)`. Line 2720 computes `scatteredLight = (msLight + silverLining) * cloud.sunIntensity`. Unlike `msLight` (which evaluates Henyey-Greenstein phase lobes based on $\cos\theta$), `silverLining` has zero dependence on the sun angle $\cos\theta$. At low density ($< 0.33$), `silverLining` reaches $\sim 1.0$, whereas `msLight` in backscatter is $\sim 0.01$.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** When viewing clouds looking directly away from the sun (anti-solar direction) or when the sun is near or below the horizon, cloud edges with density $< 0.33$ glow intensely with a bright white rim that is 70× brighter than the physically scattered light. Clouds appear backlit and glowing even when viewing their shadowed front faces.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Modulate `silverLining` by the forward-scattering phase factor: `silverLining *= max(0.0, cosTheta) * hgPhase(cosTheta, 0.9) * (4.0 * PI)`.

### H-492. Fixed Shell Midpoint Reprojection with Zero Wind Advection Causing Parallax Ghosting & Motion Smear
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/CloudTemporalResolve.wgsl:200-245`, - `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/CloudTemporalResolve.wgsl:353-380`
* **Defect Mechanism:** In the default temporal resolve path (active whenever reconstruction attachments are disabled), line 210 anchors reprojection to `0.5 * (interval.x + interval.y)` (the geometric midpoint of the planetary atmosphere shell). Furthermore, line 360 computes `previousEyeRelative = currentEyeRelative + u.cameraDeltaAndWidth.xyz`, accounting only for camera translation and ignoring cloud wind advection (`cloudWindSpeed * cloudWindDirection`).
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** For clouds near the bottom ($1500\,\text{m}$) or top ($4000\,\text{m}$) of the shell, camera movement produces massive reprojection parallax error. The 3×3 min/max neighborhood clamp fails at high-contrast cloud edges, causing severe trailing, ghosting, and smearing. When wind is active ($15\,\text{m/s}$), clouds move while the reprojection assumes static world positions, causing continuous blurring that washes out fractal Worley erosion.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Enable cloud reconstruction depth consumption by default in the temporal pass (`reconstructionDepth.g` transmittance-weighted depth), and incorporate wind advection displacement into `previousEyeRelative`: `previousEyeRelative += u.cameraDeltaAndWidth.xyz - windVelocity * deltaTime`.

### H-493. Multi-Collection Volumetric Suppression Bug
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Scene/CloudCollection.js:606-613`, - `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUContext.ts:1951-1955`, - `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts:1390-1396`
* **Defect Mechanism:** `WebGPUContext.ts:1952` implements `requestVolumetricClouds` with a first-collection-wins guard: `if (this._volumetricCloudRequest === undefined) this._volumetricCloudRequest = config;`. Any secondary collection's request is discarded. Concurrently, `WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts:1394-1396` suppresses billboard draw commands whenever `renderMode === VOLUMETRIC`.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** When an application adds two or more `CloudCollection` primitives in volumetric mode (e.g., a regional cumulus layer and an elevated cirrus deck), only the first collection renders. The secondary collection's volumetric request is ignored by `WebGPUContext`, while its billboard draw commands are suppressed by `WebGPUCloudRenderer`. The secondary collection becomes completely invisible with zero diagnostic warning.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Aggregate multiple volumetric collection requests into a multi-deck configuration payload in `WebGPUContext`, or emit a descriptive `DeveloperError` / fallback to billboard rendering for non-primary volumetric collections.

### H-494. Hard Knife-Edge Clamping and Zero 3D Tiles / Model Shadowing in Cloud Ground Shadows
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Globe/GlobeTerrain.wgsl:2448-2455`, - `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Globe/GlobeTerrain.wgsl:2430-2445`, - `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUCloudShadowFrame.ts:274-296`
* **Defect Mechanism:** `GlobeTerrain.wgsl:2452` checks `if (uv.x < 0.0 || uv.x > 1.0 || uv.y < 0.0 || uv.y > 1.0) return 1.0;`, creating a step discontinuity at the edge of the 60 km shadow footprint. In the cascade path (lines 2434-2442), cascade selection switches abruptly between $p0, p1, p2$ with zero cross-cascade blending. Furthermore, `cloudShadowMap` is only sampled in `GlobeTerrain.wgsl`, `VolumetricFog.wgsl`, and `AerialPerspective.wgsl`; 3D Tiles, glTF Models, and primitives never sample it.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Terrain displays artificial, razor-sharp rectangular shadow boundaries across valleys and mountains that shift and pop abruptly during camera translation. When clouds pass over cities (e.g., Photorealistic 3D Tiles or Cesium OSM Buildings), ground terrain is darkened while buildings, bridges, and 3D assets remain fully illuminated, creating jarring visual incoherence.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Apply smoothstep edge fading along footprint borders (`uv * (1 - uv)`), implement cross-cascade blend bands, and plumb `cloudShadowMap` into `Model.wgsl` and 3D Tiles shaders.

### H-495. Catastrophic Floating-Point Precision Cancellation in `ellipsoidShellHeightFractionRTE`
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/ProceduralClouds.wgsl:1800-1816`
* **Defect Mechanism:** Line 1810 unprojects camera-relative sample offsets back to absolute ECEF in single precision: `let worldPos = (point - centerHigh) - centerLow;`. Lines 1811-1814 then evaluate `fromInner = max(dot(innerScaled, innerScaled) - 1.0, 0.0)`. For `worldPos` magnitudes around $6.378 \times 10^6\,\text{m}$, `dot(innerScaled, innerScaled)` is $\approx 1.00047$. Subtracting $1.0$ in f32 cancels the leading 14 bits of mantissa, leaving only $\sim 10$ bits of precision ($\approx 3$ decimal digits).
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** The height fraction experiences $\sim 1\,\text{meter}$ quantization stair-stepping. In thin cloud decks (e.g. stratus layers of $500\,\text{m}$ thickness), this causes visible horizontal banding in vertical density gradients, cloud top/bottom color transitions, and ambient lighting.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Compute height fraction directly from camera-relative coordinates using the expansion $(p_{rel} - c_{scaled})^2 - 1 = p_{rel}^2 - 2 p_{rel} \cdot c_{scaled} + (c_{scaled}^2 - 1)$, eliminating the re-accumulation of absolute ECEF position in single-precision f32.

### H-496. Inappropriate Powder Effect Extinction in Multiple Scattering Octaves
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/ProceduralClouds.wgsl:2134-2137`
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `multiScatterLight`, lines 2136-2137 evaluate `let powderEffect = 1.0 - exp(-opticalDepth * absorb * 2.0 * ext)` and `let bp = mix(beer, beer * powderEffect, powder)` across every octave $i \in [0, n-1]$. In atmospheric radiative transfer, the powder effect is an empirical single-scattering approximation representing direct forward-scatter extinction near cloud boundaries. Higher octaves represent diffuse internal multi-bounce scattering where boundary forward extinction does not occur.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Near cloud tops and thin cloud edges where optical depth is low, `powderEffect` approaches 0, extinguishing higher-order multiple scattering along with direct illumination. Cloud tops and illuminated silhouettes appear excessively dark and muddy rather than bright and translucent.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Apply `powderEffect` only to octave 0:
  ```wgsl
  let bp = select(beer, mix(beer, beer * powderEffect, powder), i == 0);
  ```

### H-497. 1750-Meter Unsampled Dead Zone in `lightMarchCone` Causing Sudden Shadow Popping
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/ProceduralClouds.wgsl:1899-1925`, - `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/ProceduralClouds.wgsl:1951-1976`
* **Defect Mechanism:** In `lightMarchCone`, 5 short cone taps march from 0 up to $5 \times coneStepBase = 2000\,\text{m}$ (for a $2500\,\text{m}$ layer). The 6th far tap is sampled at a fixed distance $1.5 \times layerThickness = 3750\,\text{m}$ with a weight of $coneStepBase \times 3.0 = 1200\,\text{m}$. The interval between $2000\,\text{m}$ and $3750\,\text{m}$ ($1750\,\text{m}$ wide) is never sampled.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** When a cloud moves through the $1750\,\text{m}$ gap, it casts no shadow. The instant its edge reaches $3750\,\text{m}$, the 6th tap samples it and multiplies its density by $1200\,\text{m}$ of optical depth, causing deep, sudden black shadows to flash across clouds during wind advection or camera motion.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Distribute all 6 taps continuously across the light march interval using geometric progression ($d_i = \text{base} \times r^i$) so that sample spacing increases smoothly without dead zones.

## Part 51: Wave 17 Architectural Modernization & Performance Vectors (P2)

### M-278. Extreme Texture Sampler Saturation in Temporal AABB Neighborhood Construction
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/VolumetricFog.wgsl:1276-1279, 1308-1323`, - `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUVolumetricFogResources.ts:493-500`
* **Architectural Mechanism:** `temporalResolve` builds a 3x3x3 neighborhood AABB by executing 27 `tSampleCurrent(nc, res)` calls per voxel. `tSampleCurrent` uses `temporalSampler` with linear filtering (`textureSampleLevel`).
  For medium quality ($160 \times 90 \times 128$), this triggers $49,766,400$ trilinear fetches per frame; for high quality ($240 \times 135 \times 192$), it triggers $167,961,600$ trilinear fetches.
* **Expected Impact:** Heavy texture unit and L2 cache thrashing, consuming 2–5 ms of GPU time per frame on integrated or midrange GPUs.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Use `textureLoad(integratedCurrent, vec3<i32>(nc), 0)` to read exact neighbor texels without trilinear interpolation.

---

---

### M-279. Wasted 3D Texture Allocation and Redundant Pass 1/Pass 2 VRAM Roundtrip
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUVolumetricFogResources.ts:83-116, 173-178`, - `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/VolumetricFog.wgsl:824-924, 930-1111`
* **Architectural Mechanism:** `densityTexture` is an `rgba16float` texture (14.1 MB at medium, 47.5 MB at high), yet G and B are zero, and A stores uniform anisotropy. Furthermore, Pass 2 (`lightScattering`) reads only the exact same `gid` that Pass 1 (`densityInjection`) wrote, with zero neighbor sharing.
* **Expected Impact:** 47.5 MB of VRAM is permanently held for empty/redundant channels, and an unnecessary GPU compute pass and global VRAM memory roundtrip occur every frame.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Fuse `densityInjection` and `lightScattering` into a single compute pass. Eliminate `densityTexture` completely, saving 14–48 MB VRAM and one dispatch.

### M-280. Prefix Integral Boundary Offset Inducing Near-Plane Fog Bias
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/VolumetricFog.wgsl:1151-1196`, - `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/VolumetricFogComposite.wgsl:115-128`, - `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUVolumetricFogResources.ts:608-615`
* **Architectural Mechanism:** `integrate` stores the prefix integral from `near` to `slice(k+1)` in slice index `k`. ### M-287. Defective SIMD Feature Detection & Inoperable WASM Fallback Gates
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Core/WasmFeatureDetection.js:66-87, 149-165`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/WasmMatrixBridge.js:66, 76-78, 111, 226`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/WasmHeightmapBridge.js:91, 102-104, 141`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/WasmPointCloudBridge.js:83, 93-97, 131, 217, 309`, - `packages/wasm/src/matrix_batch.rs:57`
* **Architectural Mechanism:** 1. In `WasmMatrixBridge.js:66`, `WasmHeightmapBridge.js:91`, and `WasmPointCloudBridge.js:83`, `WasmFeatureDetection.checkSIMDSupport()` is invoked, but its return value is discarded.
  2. `_wasmReady` is set to `true` even if `_simdActive` is false.
  3. Dispatch conditions check `if (_wasmReady && count >= this._threshold)`, completely ignoring `_simdActive`.
  4. In `matrix_batch.rs:57`, the code uses `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` instead of `#[cfg(target_feature = "simd128")]`. Compiling the WASM binary for `wasm32` without SIMD flags causes compile failure on `v128` intrinsics.
* **Expected Impact:** If a non-SIMD WASM binary is deployed or SIMD is unsupported, bridges invoke SIMD WASM functions expecting scalar execution, resulting in WASM traps.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Proactively check `checkSIMDSupport()` prior to WASM fetching. Guard SIMD intrinsics in Rust with `#[cfg(target_feature = "simd128")]` and provide clean scalar fallback branches.

### M-288. Hardcoded Static Slot Limit & Inflexible Single-Arena Architecture
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/wasm/src/lib.rs:82, 101-110, 124`, - `packages/engine/Source/Scene/WasmArenaSlots.js:23-25, 29-57`
* **Architectural Mechanism:** `packages/wasm/src/lib.rs:82` hardcodes `pub const NUM_SLOTS: usize = 8;`.
  All 8 slots (0–7) are fully allocated to existing bridges (`DEFAULT`, `CULL`, `SORT`, `HEIGHTMAP`, `QUANTIZED_MESH`, `RTE`, `MATRIX`, `POINT_CLOUD`). There is zero capacity headroom. Any new bridge requesting slot 8 fails silently with null pointer returns (`ptr === 0`).

### M-295. Fragment Shader Raycast Polygon Draping vs. GPU Hardware Rasterization
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Core/VectorPipeline.js:538-655`, - `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Globe/GlobeTerrain.wgsl:4599-4680`, - `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/VectorCommon.glsl:274-312`
* **Architectural Mechanism:** Instead of utilizing GPU primitive rasterization or compute shader tessellation, Cesium drapes polygons onto terrain by performing 2D horizontal raycasts inside the globe terrain fragment shader (`vectorEdgeCrossesRay`). To support this, `VectorPipeline.packPolygonGrid` runs CPU Sutherland-Hodgman clipping (`_clipRingToRect`) to subdivide all polygon rings into grid cells with `CesiumMath.EPSILON5` margins.
* **Expected Impact:** For complex cadastral boundaries or multi-polygons with high edge density per grid cell, every rasterized fragment of the globe executes a looping ray-intersection routine. In 4K viewports, this imposes millions of redundant arithmetic operations inside the core terrain shader, driving down GPU fill rates.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Transition clamped polygon draping to use hardware stencil classification volumes (matching `WebGPUVector3DTilePrimitiveRenderer.js`) or compute-based rasterization masks into a virtual vector texture hierarchy.

### M-297. 15-Bit Quantization Precision Ceiling in Polyline Decoding
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Core/decodeVectorPolylinePositions.js:6, 33-35`
* **Architectural Mechanism:** `decodeVectorPolylinePositions.js` normalizes polyline vertices using a 15-bit signed integer divisor:
  ```js
  const maxShort = 32767;
  const lon = CesiumMath.lerp(rectangle.west, rectangle.east, u / maxShort);
  const lat = CesiumMath.lerp(rectangle.south, rectangle.north, v / maxShort);
  ```
* **Expected Impact:** At lower zoom levels (e.g. zoom 0 to 4), a tile rectangle spans thousands of kilometers. A divisor of 32,767 yields an effective spatial resolution of only 38 to 1,223 meters per step. Linear features (coastlines, state boundaries, major transmission lines) exhibit noticeable stair-stepping and quantization artifacts.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Upgrade attribute compression to 32-bit integer or uncompressed float deltas for wide-extent tiles, reserving 16-bit packing strictly for high zoom levels (Z >= 12).

### M-298. Cross-Tile Seam Gaps & Unstitched Buffer Overlaps in MVT Geometry
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Scene/buildVectorGltfFromMVT.js:958-977`
* **Architectural Mechanism:** `buildVectorGltfFromMVT.js` generates positions relative to the center of each individual tile (`origin`), casting the difference to `Float32Array`. Because adjacent tiles have differing origins, identical border vertices experience differing floating-point truncation. Furthermore, vector tile buffers (typically 64 or 128 integer units beyond `extent`) are not clipped to the tile boundary.
* **Expected Impact:** Translucent polygons render with double-opacity bands along tile boundaries where buffers overlap, while opaque meshes exhibit sub-meter cracks and T-junction flickering under varying camera angles.
* **Modernization Strategy:** Clip decoded MVT geometry exactly to `[0, extent]` when stitching is desired, or enforce shared boundary vertex snap snapping across neighbor tiles.

### M-300. Non-Deterministic Trigonometric Hash & Correlation Collapse in Compute Noise Bake
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/CloudNoiseBake.wgsl:44-62`, - `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/CloudNoiseBake.wgsl:157-159`
* **Architectural Mechanism:** `gradHash` and `featHash` rely on `fract(sin(q) * 43758.5453123)`. For large coordinates $q > 50000$, standard trigonometric implementations in GPU drivers suffer severe precision degradation. Additionally, `gradHash` and `featHash` share identical dot-product constants, making Perlin gradient directions and Worley feature point offsets collinear and correlated.
* **Expected Impact:** 
* **Modernization Strategy:** Replace trigonometric hashing with an integer bit-twiddling hash (such as PCG or MurmurHash3 integer permutations) operating on wrapped integer cell coordinates `vec3<u32>`.

### M-301. Sub-Nyquist Sampling & Box-Filter Contrast Flattening in 3D Noise Mipmaps
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/CloudNoiseBake.wgsl:268-274`, - `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/CloudNoiseMipmap.wgsl:16-52`
* **Architectural Mechanism:** The detail texture bakes frequency-16 inverted Worley noise into a 32³ grid (2 voxels per cell). In `CloudNoiseMipmap.wgsl`, downsampling uses an unweighted $2 \times 2 \times 2$ arithmetic box average (`sum * 0.125`). A linear box average across non-linear Euclidean distance fields erodes peaks and flattens contrast.

## Part 52: Wave 18 Critical Core Vulnerabilities (P0)

### C-384. Weather Precipitation Assumes Flat-Earth +Y Up in Global ECEF Space (Inverted/Sideways Fall & Immediate Global Particle Extinction)
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUWeatherRenderer.ts:307-311`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUWeatherRenderer.ts:344-345`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/WeatherParticles.wgsl:131-132`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/WeatherParticles.wgsl:171-177`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/WeatherParticles.wgsl:226-230`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/WeatherParticles.wgsl:236-240`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In Cesium, the world is a 3D WGS84 curved ellipsoid centered at `(0, 0, 0)`. The camera position `camera.positionWC` is expressed in Earth-Centered Earth-Fixed (ECEF) coordinates with magnitude $\sim 6.371 \times 10^6\text{ m}$. In ECEF, the local "Up" vector is the geodetic/geocentric surface normal $\vec{u} = \text{normalize}(\vec{p}_{\text{cam}})$, which points in arbitrary 3D directions depending on planetary latitude and longitude.
  However, `WebGPUWeatherRenderer.ts` and `WeatherParticles.wgsl` assume a flat DirectX/OpenGL coordinate system where $+Y$ is "Up", $-Y$ is gravity, and $X/Z$ is the horizontal ground plane:
  1. `WebGPUWeatherRenderer.ts` lines 307-311 hardcodes gravity to `(0, -1, 0, 9.81)` in ECEF space.
  2. `WebGPUWeatherRenderer.ts` lines 344-345 computes the ground plane relative altitude as `worldGroundAlt - currY`, where `currY` is the camera's raw ECEF Y coordinate (`frameState.camera.positionWC.y`).
  3. `WeatherParticles.wgsl` lines 226-230 emits falling particles at `p.position.y = halfExtents.y` in the ECEF frame.
  4. `WeatherParticles.wgsl` lines 236-240 initializes downward rain velocity strictly along $-Y$ (`velocity.y = -8.0 - baseSpeed * 12.0`).
  5. `WeatherParticles.wgsl` lines 174-177 kills particles whenever `p.position.y < relativeGroundAlt`.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** - **New York City / Americas:** ECEF camera $Y \approx -4.65 \times 10^6\text{ m}$. The local up vector has a negative Y component ($\approx -0.73$). Because gravity is hardcoded to $(0, -1, 0)$, $\vec{g} \cdot \vec{u} > 0$: gravity pulls rain UPWARDS away from the Earth into outer space!
  - **Immediate Particle Death:** In New York, `relativeGroundAlt = 0 - (-4,654,000) = +4,654,000`. Particles spawn with camera-relative offsets in $[-500, +500]$. On the very first simulation step, `p.position.y < relativeGroundAlt` evaluates to `true` for 100% of particles, causing total instantaneous particle extinction. Precipitation is 100% invisible across the entire Western Hemisphere.
  - **Europe / Africa (Prime Meridian):** ECEF camera $Y \approx 0$. Local Up is $(X, 0, Z)$. Gravity $(0, -1, 0)$ is perpendicular to Up, so rain falls completely sideways horizontally across the landscape.
  - **Tokyo / East Asia:** ECEF camera $Y \approx +3.35 \times 10^6\text{ m}$. `relativeGroundAlt = -3,350,000`. Particle positions never reach $-3.35 \times 10^6\text{ m}$, so ground collision never triggers, and particles fall infinitely through the Earth.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Construct the camera's local topocentric East-North-Up (ENU) rotation matrix `Transforms.eastNorthUpToFixedFrame(cameraPosition)` on the CPU. Pass the true local ellipsoidal down vector $\vec{g}_{\text{local}} = -\text{normalize}(\vec{p}_{\text{cam}})$ as `params.gravity.xyz`. In `emitParticles`, spawn particles in the camera's local ENU frame or along the camera's view frustum, and evaluate ground collision as the distance along the local normal: $(\vec{p}_{\text{particle}} \cdot \vec{u}) < (\text{groundAltitude} - \text{cameraAltitude})$.

### C-385. FFT Ocean Spectrum Violates Hermitian Symmetry in Frequency Domain (Imaginary Crosstalk Destroys Wave Height & Choppiness)
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Ocean/OceanInitialSpectrum.wgsl:71-81`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOceanRenderer.ts:217-242`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Ocean/OceanTimeSpectrum.wgsl:66-82`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Ocean/OceanIFFT.wgsl:45-48`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Ocean/OceanMerge.wgsl:64-67`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** An inverse discrete Fourier transform of a frequency spectrum produces a purely real-valued spatial field if and only if the spectrum satisfies the Hermitian condition $H(-\vec{k}) = H^*(\vec{k})$. In Tessendorf spectral ocean synthesis:
  $$h(\vec{k}, t) = h_0(\vec{k}) e^{i\omega t} + h_0^*(-\vec{k}) e^{-i\omega t}$$
  For this expression to be Hermitian, $h_0(-\vec{k})$ must be the exact same realization of the complex Gaussian random variable sampled at the mirrored frequency $-\vec{k}$ (located at texel $[(N - id.x) \bmod N, (N - id.y) \bmod N]$).
  In `OceanInitialSpectrum.wgsl` lines 71-78:
  ```wgsl
  let noise = textureLoad(Noise, vec2<i32>(id.xy), 0);
  let h0 = invSqrt2 * noise.xy * sqrt(phillips(k));
  let hm = invSqrt2 * noise.zw * sqrt(phillips(-k));
  let h0MinusConj = vec2<f32>(hm.x, -hm.y);
  ```
  `noise.zw` is loaded from `id.xy`, which `WebGPUOceanRenderer.ts` lines 236-239 populates with two independent Box-Muller random variables. It is completely uncorrelated with the noise sampled at $-\vec{k}$.
  Therefore, $h(\vec{k}, t)$ is NOT Hermitian, and its IFFT has a non-zero imaginary component.
  In `OceanTimeSpectrum.wgsl` line 79, the shader packs $g_1 = Dy + i Dx$. By linearity:
  $$\mathcal{F}^{-1}(g_1) = (\text{Re}(Dy) - \text{Im}(Dx)) + i (\text{Im}(Dy) + \text{Re}(Dx))$$
  In `OceanMerge.wgsl` lines 64-66, the real part is extracted as height $Dy = \text{Re}(g_1)$ and the imaginary part as horizontal displacement $Dx = \text{Im}(g_1)$.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** The synthesized wave height $Dy$ is corrupted by the imaginary leak of horizontal choppiness $Dx$, and horizontal choppiness $Dx$ is corrupted by the imaginary leak of wave height $Dy$. The ocean exhibits destructive phase cancellation, non-physical wave spikes, missing wave energy, and chaotic cross-talk between horizontal pinch and vertical displacement. In `FieldDz`, $Dz$ is similarly non-Hermitian; its imaginary component is discarded in `OceanMerge.wgsl` line 67, permanently losing half of the lateral wave energy.
* **Architectural Remediation:** In `OceanInitialSpectrum.wgsl`, populate $h_0(\vec{k})$ using `noise.xy` sampled at `id.xy`. Sample $h_0(-\vec{k})$ from `(params.size - id.x) % params.size, (params.size - id.y) % params.size`, and take its complex conjugate. This strictly guarantees $h(-\vec{k}, t) = h^*(\vec{k}, t)$ so that $\text{Im}(Dy) \equiv 0$ and $\text{Im}(Dx) \equiv 0$, preventing any cross-channel contamination during two-for-one IFFT reassembly.

### C-386. Pseudo-RTE 64-Bit Precision Breakdown in Flow-Field Advection (`lonLatToEcef` FP32 Precision Catastrophe)
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/FlowFieldRender.wgsl:57-64`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/FlowFieldRender.wgsl:83-88`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUFlowFieldRenderer.ts:470-474`, `AGENTS.md: Part One, Rule 1`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** `FlowFieldRender.wgsl` claims to implement 64-bit RTE emulated precision, but evaluates geodetic coordinate conversion entirely in single-precision FP32:
  ```wgsl
  let pos = lonLatToEcef(p.x, p.y, render.heightOffset);
  let high = floor(pos / 65536.0) * 65536.0;
  let low = pos - high;
  ```
  In `lonLatToEcef` lines 60-62, `render.radiiSquared` is $(6378137.0)^2 \approx 4.068 \times 10^{13} > 2^{45}$. In IEEE 754 32-bit float (24 mantissa bits), machine epsilon at $4 \times 10^{13}$ is $2^{21} \approx 2.1 \times 10^6$! The resulting `surface` vector at $6.378 \times 10^6\text{ m}$ is quantized to $\sim 0.5 - 1.0\text{ m}$ grid steps. Performing `floor(pos / 65536.0) * 65536.0` on an already-quantized FP32 vector cannot restore the destroyed precision.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Direct violation of `AGENTS.md` Rule 1. When the camera zooms in to low altitude (e.g. city scale, mountain valleys, or coastal framing), wind particles jitter and snap violently across a 0.5-meter quantization grid, completely breaking smooth streamflow animation.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Do not materialize absolute ECEF positions in FP32. Pass the camera's geodetic cartographic position $(\lambda_{\text{cam}}, \phi_{\text{cam}}, h_{\text{cam}})$ and evaluate particle positions relative to the camera in the local East-North-Up (ENU) frame:
  $$\Delta \vec{p}_{\text{ENU}} = \begin{pmatrix} R_{\text{east}} \cdot (\lambda - \lambda_{\text{cam}}) \cos \phi \\ R_{\text{north}} \cdot (\phi - \phi_{\text{cam}}) \\ h - h_{\text{cam}} \end{pmatrix}$$
  Transform $\Delta \vec{p}_{\text{ENU}}$ directly to eye space via the camera's view matrix, preserving sub-millimeter precision at all zoom levels.

### C-387. WebGPU Validation Abort from Incompatible Attachment Sample Counts in OIT Accumulation Pass under MSAA
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:136-161`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:206-224`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.ts:193-207`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:741-746`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `WebGPUOIT.update` (`WebGPUOIT.ts:206-224`), `_accumulationTexture` (`rgba16float`) and `_revealageTexture` (`r8unorm`) are allocated without specifying `sampleCount`, defaulting strictly to `1`. However, in `executeTranslucentPass` (`WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.ts:193-207`), `accPassDesc` is requested via `host._oit.getAccumulationPassDescriptor(depthView)`, where `depthView` is the scene framebuffer's depth-stencil view (`host._sceneFramebuffer.colorTarget.getDepthStencilTextureView()`). When the scene framebuffer is multisampled (e.g., `sampleCount = 4`), `depthView` has `sampleCount = 4`.
  Per WebGPU Specification (§9.1 GPURenderPassDescriptor): *"All attachments (both color attachments and the depth-stencil attachment) must have matching sample counts."* Passing a 1x color attachment with a 4x depth attachment causes `device.createCommandEncoder().beginRenderPass(...)` to immediately fail WebGPU validation, invalidating the command encoder, dropping the frame, and cascading into device lost.
  Furthermore, `createOITPipeline` (`WebGPUOIT.ts:745`) forwards `multisample: config.multisample`. An MSAA draw command produces an OIT pipeline with `multisample.count = 4`, which subsequently violates render pass pipeline compatibility when bound in a 1x accumulation render pass.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** A user enables anti-aliasing (`viewer.scene.msaaSamples = 4`) and activates WebGPU OIT (`viewer.scene.debugShowWebGPUOIT = true` or `CesiumDebug.webgpuOIT`). The moment any translucent model, building, or particle system enters the frustum, the browser throws:
  `[WebGPU Validation Error]: Color attachment sample count (1) does not match DepthStencil attachment sample count (4)`.
  The render loop crashes, leading to a black viewport.
* **Architectural Remediation:** 1. Allocate `_accumulationTexture` and `_revealageTexture` with `sampleCount: this._sampleCount`.
  2. If accumulation and revealage are multisampled, provide transient MSAA targets and resolve targets, or alternatively, resolve the scene depth to a single-sampled depth texture before opening the accumulation pass so that accumulation, revealage, and depth attachments are all uniformly `sampleCount: 1`.
  3. Ensure `createOITPipeline` forces `multisample.count` to match the actual accumulation pass render target sample count.

### C-388. Logarithmic Depth Stripping in OIT Fragment Return Causing Severe Depth Test Rejection & Z-Fighting
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:437-441`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:616-643`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOIT.ts:669-676`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Model/ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2377-2382`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2377-2382`, when `LOG_DEPTH` is enabled, the fragment output structure declares:
  ```wgsl
  struct FragOutput {
    @location(0) color: vec4<f32>,
    @location(1) normalRoughness: vec4<f32>,
    @builtin(frag_depth) depth: f32,
  };
  ```
  `@builtin(frag_depth)` is essential: it writes the logarithmic depth value required to compare correctly against the logarithmic depth buffer populated by the opaque globe and 3D tiles.
  However, in `WebGPUOIT.ts:616-643`, `_stripStructIOAttributes` systematically strips all `@builtin(...)` and `@location(...)` attributes from the original return structure so that `_oit_base_fragmentMain` can return a clean struct. Then, in `_injectOITStructReturn` (`WebGPUOIT.ts:670-675`), the new entry point returns `OITFragOutput`:
  ```wgsl
  struct OITFragOutput {
    @location(0) accumulation: vec4<f32>,
    @location(1) revealage: vec4<f32>,
  }
  ```
  `OITFragOutput` completely omits `@builtin(frag_depth)`! Consequently, WebGPU falls back to the rasterized hardware window depth (`position.z`). The accumulation pass then executes depth testing (`less-equal`) using non-linear hardware window depth against a depth buffer that was written with logarithmic depth ($\frac{\log(z + 1)}{\log(far + 1)}$). Because hardware depth and logarithmic depth possess radically divergent non-linear distributions, translucent fragments are falsely rejected by the depth test or experience massive z-fighting against terrain and models.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** A translucent glTF building or translucent photogrammetry mesh is rendered over terrain with logarithmic depth enabled (Cesium's default). Because the fragment's logarithmic depth calculation is stripped by OIT injection, the GPU compares hardware depth against logarithmic terrain depth. The translucent model is prematurely clipped and vanishes beneath the terrain or flickers violently as the camera pans.
* **Architectural Remediation:** 1. Inspect the base shader for `@builtin(frag_depth)`. If present, define `OITFragOutputWithDepth`:
     ```wgsl
     struct OITFragOutput {
       @location(0) accumulation: vec4<f32>,
       @location(1) revealage: vec4<f32>,
       @builtin(frag_depth) depth: f32,
     }
     ```
  2. In `_injectOITStructReturn`, preserve and forward the computed depth value (`_oitBase.depth`) to the return struct.

### C-389. Severe Translucent Pick Inversion: Front-to-Back Sort with Disabled Depth Writes Causes Farthest Object to Win
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts:768-777`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:1351-1356`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:1400`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts:768-777`:
  ```typescript
  const translucentCount = frustumCommands.indices[Pass.TRANSLUCENT] ?? 0;
  if (translucentCount > 1) {
    sortCommandsFrontToBack(
      frustumCommands.commands[Pass.TRANSLUCENT],
      translucentCount,
      scene,
    );
  }
  execute(Pass.TRANSLUCENT);
  ```
  The translucent pick commands are sorted **front-to-back**.
  However, in `WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:1400` (and corresponding primitive pick pipeline builders), the depth state is configured with:
  ```typescript
  depthWriteEnabled: !isBlend // false for translucent commands
  ```
  In the pick render pass, blending is disabled (the shader writes a 32-bit pick ID). Because `depthWriteEnabled` is `false`, each translucent command that passes the depth test against opaque geometry unconditionally overwrites the color buffer with its pick ID.
  Because commands are sorted front-to-back, the nearest translucent object renders *first*. Then, the second-nearest translucent object renders and *overwrites* the pixel. Finally, the farthest translucent object renders and *overwrites* all preceding objects.
  This directly inverts pick priority: the farthest translucent object always wins the pick.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** A user views a 3D architectural model featuring a glass curtain wall in front of interior translucent partitions. The user clicks on the outer glass window to inspect its properties. Because the outer window was drawn first and the inner partition was drawn second without depth writes, the pick pass registers the inner partition ID. The application inspects the wrong entity.
* **Architectural Remediation:** 1. For translucent pick passes without alpha blending, either:
     - Enable `depthWriteEnabled: true` on the pick pipeline so front-to-back rendering causes nearer translucent surfaces to occlude farther ones; OR
     - If depth writing must remain off to allow picking opaque geometry behind translucent objects, sort translucent commands **back-to-front** so that nearer translucent objects draw last and overwrite farther ones.

### C-390. WebGPU Command Encoder Finish/Submit Failure Leaves Ring Buffer Slots Permanently Locked (`readbackPending = true`) and Leaks Pending Submissions
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUTimestampProfiler.ts:518-522`:, state.readbackPending = true;, this._pendingSubmissions.push({, stateIndex: this._currentFrameIndex,, generation: this._currentFrameGeneration,, });, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUTimestampProfiler.ts:411-416`:, const state = this._frameStates[this._currentFrameIndex];, this._currentFrameAvailable =, !state.readbackPending && state.readbackBuffer.mapState === "unmapped";, if (!this._currentFrameAvailable) {, this._readbackSkipCount++;, }, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUContext.ts:3388, 3403-3411, 3446-3462`:, this._performanceManager?.endFrame(this._currentCommandEncoder); // :3388, ..., const commandBuffer = submittedEncoder.finish();                 // :3403, this._device.queue.submit([commandBuffer]);                      // :3404, ..., this._timestampProfiler?.afterSubmit();                          // :3411, ..., } catch (error) {                                                // :3446, this._drainAfterCommandEncoderSubmitCallbacks(false);, this._drainAfterFrameSubmitCallbacks(false);, ..., throw error;, }
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** When `WebGPUContext.endFrame` executes, `_performanceManager.endFrame(encoder)` invokes `timestampProfiler.endFrame(encoder)` *before* the command buffer is finished and submitted. In `timestampProfiler.endFrame`, `state.readbackPending` is set to `true` and the submission is appended to `this._pendingSubmissions`. If an unhandled validation error, out-of-memory error, or exception occurs during `submittedEncoder.finish()` (line 3403), `_submitPendingTextureMipJobs()`, or `device.queue.submit()` (line 3404), execution diverts to the `catch` block (lines 3446–3462). The `catch` block settles submit callbacks and uniform allocators, but **never notifies `timestampProfiler`** that the submission was aborted. Consequently, `afterSubmit()` is never called, `this._pendingSubmissions` retains the orphaned entry, and `state.readbackPending` remains `true` indefinitely.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** During scene rendering, a transient shader pipeline error or texture allocation failure throws in `finish()` or `queue.submit()`. When the rendering recovers on the next frame, the profiler ring advances. After `_bufferCount` (3) frames, the ring returns to the slot that encountered the abort. Because `state.readbackPending` remains permanently `true`, `_currentFrameAvailable` evaluates to `false` every time that slot is visited (`readbackSkipCount` increments indefinitely). If 3 transient errors occur over an entire session, all 3 ring slots become permanently locked out, `ringSaturated` becomes permanently `true`, and timestamp profiling ceases to function completely without an explicit `reset()`.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Introduce an explicit abort/rollback hook `abortFrame()` on `WebGPUTimestampProfiler` (and `WebGPUPerformanceManager`). In `WebGPUContext.ts:3446` `catch (error)`, invoke `this._performanceManager?.abortFrame()` or `this._timestampProfiler?.abortFrame()`. In `abortFrame()`, pop or clear the pending submission for the active slot, restore `state.readbackPending = false`, and account the attempt as `lost` or `failed` in the sample ledger rather than stranding the ring slot.

---

### C-391. `setBufferCount()` Resource Leak for In-Flight Unsettled Submissions
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUTimestampProfiler.ts:965-971`:, const retiring = this._frameStates;, this._frameStates = [];, this._pendingSubmissions = [];, this._bufferCount = next;, this.reset();, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUTimestampProfiler.ts:980-988`:, for (const state of retiring) {, if (state.readbackPending) {, this._retiredStates.add(state);, continue;, }, state.querySet.destroy();, state.resolveBuffer.destroy();, state.readbackBuffer.destroy();, }, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUTimestampProfiler.ts:718-727`:, if (this._retiredStates.delete(state) && !this._isDestroyed) {, state.querySet.destroy();, state.resolveBuffer.destroy();, state.readbackBuffer.destroy();, }
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** `setBufferCount` resizes the ring buffer while tracking in-flight readback slots in `this._retiredStates`. However, line 969 unconditionally clears `this._pendingSubmissions = []`. If `setBufferCount()` is called after `endFrame()` but before `afterSubmit()`, or if an encoded submission was pending dispatch to `afterSubmit()`, `state.readbackPending` is `true`. Lines 981–983 add `state` to `this._retiredStates`. But because `this._pendingSubmissions` was wiped out, `_readSubmittedFrame` will **never be invoked** for that state. Because `_readSubmittedFrame` is never executed, its `finally` block (lines 718–727), which is the **sole mechanism** for deleting and destroying states from `_retiredStates`, never executes.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Dynamic profiling tools or automated performance monitors adjust the profiler depth dynamically (e.g., expanding from 3 to 6 upon detecting ring saturation). If a resize happens before `afterSubmit()` processes the previous frame's encoded copy, the retired GPU query set, resolve buffer, and readback buffer are leaked into `_retiredStates` permanently. They are never unmapped, never resolved, and never destroyed until the entire `WebGPUTimestampProfiler` instance is destroyed.
* **Architectural Remediation:** In `setBufferCount()`, do not drop `_pendingSubmissions` without clearing `readbackPending` or explicitly destroying unsubmitted slots. For slots in `retiring` where `readbackPending === true` but no active `mapAsync` has actually started (i.e. `submission` was still in `_pendingSubmissions` and not in `_activeReadbacks`), immediately destroy `state.querySet`, `state.resolveBuffer`, and `state.readbackBuffer` instead of sequestering them in `_retiredStates`.

### C-392. Secondary Viewport Split-Submission Omits Query Set Resolution and Leaves Split Timestamps Dangling
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUContext.ts:2408, 2430-2439`:, override beginSecondaryViewport(): void {, ..., const firstViewportEncoder = this._currentCommandEncoder;, const firstViewportBuffer = firstViewportEncoder.finish();, this._device.queue.submit([firstViewportBuffer]);, this._currentCommandEncoder = null;, this._drainCommandEncoderSubmitCallbacks(firstViewportEncoder, true);, this._currentCommandEncoder = this._device.createCommandEncoder({, label: "Secondary Viewport Continuation Encoder",, });, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUContext.ts:3388, 3404, 3411`:, this._performanceManager?.endFrame(this._currentCommandEncoder);
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** When rendering Scene2D in multi-viewport / wrapped mode, `beginSecondaryViewport()` ends the first viewport's render pass, finishes `firstViewportEncoder`, and submits it directly to `device.queue` at line 2432. Any render passes recorded in the first viewport (globe, raster tiles, vector layers) attached `timestampWrites` referencing the current frame's `GPUQuerySet`. However, `firstViewportEncoder` does **not** resolve the query set. `endFrame` is only called at line 3388 on the `Secondary Viewport Continuation Encoder`.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** 1. If `beginSecondaryViewport()` throws or catches an error at line 2440, the first command buffer was already submitted to the GPU, but the continuation encoder is never created or finished. The querySet written by the GPU is never resolved, `endFrame()` never runs, and `afterSubmit()` is never called.
  2. If the secondary viewport contains no timed passes, `state.queryCount` only reflects the first viewport's passes, but the resolution and readback copy occur on a separate command buffer across a queue submission boundary. If GPU workload reordering or submission timing differs across browsers, timestamps between viewports can result in out-of-order execution artifacts.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Track whether timestamp queries were written during the first viewport segment. If `beginSecondaryViewport()` fails or aborts, ensure the profiler handles the split-submission boundary cleanly. Alternatively, resolve the first viewport's timestamp queries into the resolve buffer prior to `firstViewportEncoder.finish()`, or formalize multi-encoder timestamp resolution lifecycle support in `WebGPUTimestampProfiler`.

### C-393. Bitonic Sort Block Direction Bug in `PointCloudSort.wgsl` Breaks Global Merge
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/PointCloudSort.wgsl:85`, Contrast with fix in `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/BitonicSortU64.wgsl:88-100`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `PointCloudSort.wgsl:85`, the sort direction within the local workgroup phase is determined by:
  ```wgsl
  let ascending = (localIdx & k) == 0u;
  ```
  Within a 256-thread workgroup, `localIdx` $\in [0, 255]$. In the final local sort stage where $k = 256$, `localIdx & 256` evaluates to `0` for *every* thread in *every* workgroup. Consequently, every 256-element workgroup sorts strictly ascending. 
  Batcher's bitonic merge network requires that adjacent 256-element blocks alternate between ascending and descending order to form a 512-element bitonic sequence before entering the global merge phase ($k \ge 512$). Because all blocks sort ascending, the input to `globalBitonicMerge` is not bitonic. Empirical Monte Carlo simulation over randomized arrays confirmed that `PointCloudSort.wgsl` produces an unsorted array in **100% of runs** for $N > 256$.
  Notably, `BitonicSortU64.wgsl:88-100` correctly resolved this with `let ascending = (globalIdx & k) == 0u;`, but `PointCloudSort.wgsl` was left unpatched.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Any point cloud or splat set with $>256$ elements sorted via `PointCloudSort` is output in an invalid, scrambled order, destroying back-to-front transparency blending and causing severe visual flickering and occluded point popping.
* **Architectural Remediation:** In `PointCloudSort.wgsl:85`, replace:
  ```wgsl
  let ascending = (localIdx & k) == 0u;
  ```
  with:
  ```wgsl
  let ascending = (globalIdx & k) == 0u;
  ```
  where `globalIdx = wid.x * 256u + localIdx;`.

---

### C-394. Uniform Parameter Clobbering Across Passes in `WebGPUPointCloudSortDispatcher.ts`
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPointCloudSortDispatcher.ts:326-330`, `371-383`, Contrast with `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUGPUSortKeysDispatcher.ts:108-119`, `407-418`, `568-596`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `WebGPUPointCloudSortDispatcher.ts:371-383`, `_encodeGlobalPhases` iterates through the bitonic merge hierarchy ($k=512 \dots N, j=k/2 \dots 1$):
  ```ts
  for (let k = 512; k <= N; k <<= 1) {
    for (let j = k >> 1; j > 0; j >>= 1) {
      this._writeParams(r, N, k, j);
      const pass = encoder.beginComputePass(...);
      ...
    }
  }
  ```
  Inside `_writeParams` (lines 326-330), it executes `this._device.queue.writeBuffer(r.paramsBuffer, 0, this._paramsScratch.buffer)`.
  In WebGPU, `queue.writeBuffer` operations execute on the queue timeline prior to command buffer execution. Writing to offset 0 of `paramsBuffer` repeatedly inside the CPU encoding loop overwrites the single uniform buffer memory location. When the command buffer is submitted to the GPU, **every single global merge pass reads the exact same parameters written by the final iteration** ($k=N, j=1$). All intermediate $(k, j)$ merge steps are bypassed.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** The GPU runs $O(\log^2 N)$ passes with identical, incorrect parameters. The merge network fails entirely, leaving the buffer unsorted.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Adopt the dynamic uniform buffer offset pattern from `WebGPUGPUSortKeysDispatcher.ts`: allocate a params buffer strided by 256 bytes (`SORT_PARAMS_STRIDE`), pre-write all stage parameters into distinct offsets in a single `writeBuffer` before the pass loop, and bind `paramsBuffer` with dynamic offsets (`hasDynamicOffset: true`) during `pass.setBindGroup(0, r.bindGroup, [stageOffset])`.

---

### C-395. Non-Uniform Scale Decomposition Destroys 3D Covariance in `GaussianSplatPrimitive.transformTile`
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Scene/GaussianSplatPrimitive.js:2159-2180`, `2220-2239`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** When a tile transform possesses non-uniform scaling or shear (`useFastPath` is false), lines 2220-2239 attempt to separate the composite transform $M = T \cdot R_{parent} \cdot S_{parent} \cdot R_{splat} \cdot S_{splat}$ back into independent quaternion rotation and scale attributes:
  ```js
  Matrix4.fromTranslationQuaternionRotationScale(position, rotation, scale, scratchMatrix4D);
  Matrix4.multiplyTransformation(transform, scratchMatrix4D, scratchMatrix4D);
  Matrix4.getTranslation(scratchMatrix4D, position);
  Matrix4.getScale(scratchMatrix4D, scale);
  Quaternion.multiply(scratchTransformQuat, rotation, rotation);
  Quaternion.normalize(rotation, rotation);
  ```
  In 3D Gaussian Splatting, the 3D covariance is $\Sigma = R S^2 R^T$. Under affine transformation $A$, the covariance transforms as $\Sigma' = A \Sigma A^T$. When $A$ has non-uniform scaling, $S_{parent}$ does not commute with $R_{splat}$ ($S_{parent} R_{splat} \ne R_{splat} S_{parent}$). The resulting transformed Gaussian has principal axes rotated to an angle determined by the polar decomposition / SVD of $A R S$, not $R_{parent} R_{splat}$. Decoupling the transformation into `Quaternion.multiply(scratchTransformQuat, rotation)` and `Matrix4.getScale(scratchMatrix4D, scale)` is mathematically false and discards rotational shear.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** In 3D Tilesets where tiles have non-uniform scaling (e.g., vertical terrain exaggeration, non-uniform root scaling, or oblique georeferencing frames), Gaussian splats are rendered warped, misshapen, and rotated in directions completely misaligned with the geometry.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Transform the 3D covariance directly as a symmetric 3x3 tensor $\Sigma' = A \Sigma A^T$ in the WASM texture generator, or compute the exact rotation via SVD of $M = A R S$ rather than multiplying quaternions independently of non-uniform scale.

### C-396. Invalid Depth Texture Binding SampleType Crashing WebGPU Pipeline in Single-Sample Mode
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUHeatShimmerEffect.ts:213-218`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/HeatShimmer.wgsl:47-48`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUColdOpticsEffect.ts:255-260`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/ColdOptics.wgsl:90-91`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:3292`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPURenderTarget.ts:239-242, 501-510`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** `WebGPUHeatShimmerEffect` and `WebGPUColdOpticsEffect` declare their depth bind group entry using `texture(1, Stage.FRAGMENT)`, which defaults to `sampleType: "float"`. Their WGSL shaders declare `@binding(1) var sceneDepthTex: texture_2d<f32>;` and sample it using a standard filtering sampler (`texSampler`).
  At runtime, `WebGPUSceneRenderer` provides `context._depthStencilView` (`_sceneFramebuffer.depthSampleableView`). In single-sample mode (the engine's default non-MSAA rendering path), `WebGPURenderTarget.getDepthSampleableView()` returns `this._depthSampleableView`, which is a view created directly from the depth attachment with format `depth24plus` (or `depth32float`).
  Under the WebGPU Specification (§5.5, §13.3):
  1. A `depth24plus` texture view has `sampleType: "depth"` and CANNOT be bound to a bind group layout entry with `sampleType: "float"`.
  2. A depth texture must be declared in WGSL as `texture_depth_2d`, not `texture_2d<f32>`.
  3. Pairing a depth texture with a `"filtering"` sampler triggers an immediate WebGPU validation exception: *"depth-only texture must be paired with non-filtering sampler"*.
  Furthermore, `ColdOpticsEffect:314` uses `depthBinding = depthView ?? sourceView;`. Even if the layout were patched to `sampleType: "depth"`, falling back to `sourceView` (`bgra8unorm` / `rgba16float`) causes a reciprocal validation failure.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Whenever heat shimmer or cold optics is enabled on a non-MSAA scene, `device.createBindGroup` or `executePass` throws a fatal WebGPU validation error: `[Invalid TextureBinding] Texture binding view format (depth24plus) is incompatible with sampleType (float)`. The WebGPU device logs a validation error, drops the command buffer, and causes a complete canvas freeze/blackout.
* **Architectural Remediation:** 1. Unify depth sampling across all post-process shaders: either route all single-sample depth through a dedicated resolve/copy pass (as done in `DepthResolveMSAA.wgsl` producing `r16float` / `r32float`), or update `WebGPUHeatShimmerEffect` and `WebGPUColdOpticsEffect` bind group layouts to declare `texture(1, Stage.FRAGMENT, { sampleType: "depth" })` paired with `sampler(..., "non-filtering")`, update the WGSL declaration to `texture_depth_2d`, and use `textureLoad` / `textureSampleCompare`.
  2. Replace `depthBinding = depthView ?? sourceView` with a dedicated 1x1 zero depth fallback texture (`depth24plus` or `r16float`).

---

### C-397. Inverted Sun Perspective Divide Projecting Rear Sun Flares Centered On-Screen
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts:1276-1281`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/LensFlare.wgsl:115-124`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In `computeLensFlareFrameContext`, the sun's clip-space coordinates are computed via `viewProjection * sunPositionWC`. Perspective division is then executed unconditionally:
  ```ts
  const cw = vp[3] * sun.x + vp[7] * sun.y + vp[11] * sun.z + vp[15];
  if (cw !== 0 && isFinite(cw)) {
    frame.sunNDC = [cx / cw, cy / cw];
  }
  ```
  When the sun is located behind the camera plane ($z_{eye} < 0$), $cw < 0$. In homogeneous perspective projection, dividing by a negative $w$ projects points behind the camera through the origin into the front half-space. If the camera looks directly away from the sun, $cx \approx 0, cy \approx 0, cw < 0$, resulting in `frame.sunNDC = [0.0, 0.0]`.
  In `LensFlare.wgsl`, the screen-space gate only evaluates:
  ```wgsl
  if (!isSpace || !(sunPos.x >= -1.1 && sunPos.x <= 1.1 && sunPos.y >= -1.1 && sunPos.y <= 1.1)) {
    return originalColor;
  }
  ```
  It never checks whether $cw > 0$ or whether the sun is in the forward frustum.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** When an observer in orbital space view looks directly away from the sun (e.g., viewing night-side terrain or deep space), a brilliant, high-intensity lens flare phantom suddenly appears dead-center in the viewport.
* **Architectural Remediation:** In `computeLensFlareFrameContext`, reject rear-hemisphere projections by requiring `cw > 0.001`:
  ```ts
  if (cw > 0.001 && isFinite(cw)) {
    frame.sunNDC = [cx / cw, cy / cw];
  } else {
    frame.sunNDC = [-999.0, -999.0]; // off-screen sentinel
  }
  ```

---

### C-398. Multi-Frustum Slice Depth Clears Corrupting Heat Shimmer & Cold Optics
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.ts:218-228`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/ColdOptics.wgsl:243-249`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/HeatShimmer.wgsl:135-142`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** Cesium renders multi-frustum scenes from far to near ($i = N-1 \dots 0$). At each frustum slice, line 228 calls `host._clearDepthStencil(context)`. While color accumulates across frustums via `loadOp: "load"`, depth is cleared on every slice to avoid near-slice occlusion artifacts.
  Consequently, when execution exits the frustum loop and enters post-processing, `_sceneFramebuffer.depthSampleableView` contains depth geometry ONLY from the closest frustum slice (Frustum 0). All pixels belonging to terrain, mountains, 3D tiles, and city models in farther frustum slices have been cleared to $1.0$ (far plane).
  1. In `ColdOptics.wgsl:247`: `if (rawDepth < skyCutoff) { return sceneColor; }`. Because all distant mountains and buildings in Frustum 1+ have `rawDepth == 1.0 >= skyCutoff`, the shader classifies all distant geometry as sky, drawing ice halos and sun dogs directly over mountains and buildings.
  2. In `HeatShimmer.wgsl:138-142`: `linearizeDepth(1.0)` evaluates to `far` (100,000,000 m). Any configured `depthFadeFar` causes all distant terrain to completely lose shimmer distortion.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** In wide-area geographic views with mountains or cities located >1 km from the camera, 22° cold halos and sun dogs erroneously render across the faces of mountains and skyscrapers. Heat shimmer abruptly ceases at the Frustum 0 boundary.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Maintain a composite multi-frustum depth buffer or use the depth-plane texture / `GlobeDepth` composite texture (`context._globeDepthTexture`) where depth values across all frustum slices are preserved in logarithmic / linear space, rather than sampling the cleared single-frustum hardware depth attachment.

---

### C-399. Division by Zero & Contrast Singularity in `BrightPass.wgsl`
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/BrightPass.wgsl:81-83`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUBloomEffect.ts:46, 155, 498`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** `BrightPass.wgsl` implements the contrast formula:
  ```wgsl
  let factor = (259.0 * (contrast + 255.0)) / (255.0 * (259.0 - contrast));
  sceneColor = factor * (sceneColor - vec3<f32>(0.5)) + vec3<f32>(0.5);
  ```
  `contrast` is a runtime uniform configured via `BloomConfig.contrast` (default 128.0). If an application, animation curve, or UI slider sets `contrast = 259.0`, the denominator becomes `255.0 * 0.0 = 0.0`, resulting in division by zero and generating `+Infinity` / `NaN` across every pixel. If `contrast > 259.0`, `factor` flips to a negative number, inverting scene luminance.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Adjusting the bloom contrast slider to 259 causes the entire screen to flash black or white with NaN buffer corruption.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Clamp `contrast` to safe bounds `clamp(contrast, -254.0, 258.0)` or guard the denominator with `max(259.0 - contrast, 1e-4)`.

### C-400. Hardware MSAA Box-Filter Resolve Corrupts Packed Depth and Discrete Feature IDs
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEdgeFramebuffer.ts:127-133`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEdgeFramebuffer.ts:160-175`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEdgeFramebuffer.ts:198-212`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Model/ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:1966-1976`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Model/ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2002-2009`, Reference WebGL Contrast: `packages/engine/Source/Scene/EdgeFramebuffer.js:70` (`1, // No MSAA`)
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** `WebGPUEdgeFramebuffer` allocates a 3-target Multiple Render Target (MRT) framebuffer matching the scene sample count (`sampleCount = numSamples`):
  - Attachment 0: edge color (`colorFormat`)
  - Attachment 1: edge id + metadata (`rgba8unorm`)
  - Attachment 2: packed depth via `czm_packDepth` (`rgba8unorm`)
  When MSAA is active (`numSamples > 1`), `buildColorAttachments()` binds hardware resolve targets (`this._resolveViews[i]`) across all 3 MRT attachments. WebGPU hardware resolve executes an unweighted arithmetic box-filter averaging sub-pixel samples.
  1. *Packed Depth Corruption:* `czm_packDepth` stores depth across RGBA channels using base-255 radix weights. Linearly averaging these packed bytes across geometric edge silhouettes with clear background `vec4(0.0)` produces completely nonsensical depth bytes upon unpack (`unpackEdgeDepth`). `linearizeWindowDepth` evaluates to erroneous distances differing by hundreds of meters, causing `depthDelta >= eps` to fail and annihilating all edge pixels along silhouette boundaries.
  2. *Feature ID Corruption:* Attachment 1 stores discrete integer feature IDs in `.g` and `.b`. Resolving edge pixels with clear background scales integer values proportionally to subpixel coverage (e.g. ID 10 with 50% sample coverage becomes 5), breaking `featuresMatch` in `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl:2008`.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** On any display with MSAA enabled (2x or 4x), turning on 3D Tile edge visibility causes model edges to disappear, flicker violently, or falsely map to random feature IDs whenever edges partially intersect a screen pixel.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Decouple `WebGPUEdgeFramebuffer` from the scene MSAA sample count. In accordance with WebGL `EdgeFramebuffer.js:70`, enforce `sampleCount = 1` for all edge MRT attachments. If multisampled edge rasterization is required, resolve depth using custom custom min-depth/sample-0 resolve passes (`textureLoad` sample 0) rather than hardware color resolve targets.

### C-401. `NPROutlines.wgsl` Depth Thresholding Inverts Distance Invariance Due to Assumed Reversed-Z, Dividing by Near-Zero NDC Depth
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/NPROutlines.wgsl:77-83`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/NPROutlines.wgsl:131-143`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUNPROutlineEffect.ts:167-171`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** `NPROutlines.wgsl:135-138` computes scaled depth gradient using:
  ```wgsl
  // Scale so the threshold is a fraction of the center depth value.
  // Depth in [0,1] near→1, far→1−ε, so dividing makes the test
  // distance-invariant.
  let depthGradScaled = maxDepthGrad / max(centerDepth, 1e-6);
  ```
  The author explicitly coded for Reversed-Z (`near→1, far→1−ε`). However, Cesium WebGPU operates with standard NDC depth (`depthClearValue: 1.0`, near plane maps to $0.0$, far plane maps to $1.0$).
  For geometry in the near field, `centerDepth` approaches $0.0$ (e.g. $0.0005$). Dividing `maxDepthGrad` by near-zero depth multiplies depth noise by $1{,}000\times$ to $10{,}000\times$, completely overwhelming `uniforms.params.y` ($0.02$) and painting solid black noise over foreground terrain and buildings. Conversely, at far distances where `centerDepth \approx 1.0`, division by $1.0$ fails to compensate for hyperbolic perspective depth compression, completely blinding the edge detector.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** When `scene.enableNPROutlines = true`, any close-up inspection of assets (cockpit views, street-level 3D tiles, ground primitives) results in massive black splotches and false-positive depth edges across smooth surfaces.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Reconstruct linear view-space depth ($z_{eye}$) prior to gradient computation, or scale `maxDepthGrad` by linear depth derived from frustum parameters (`(2.0 * near * far) / (far + near - z_ndc * (far - near))`). Replace division by raw non-linear NDC depth with linear derivative scaling (`fwidth(linearZ)`).

### C-402. Complete Absence of RTE Precision on `WebGPUEdgeVisibilityEmitter` Pipeline Violating Fork Charter Precision Rule 1
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEdgeVisibilityEmitter.ts:76-80`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEdgeVisibilityEmitter.ts:133-134`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEdgeVisibilityEmitter.ts:160-167`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:8754-8757`, Fork Rule: `AGENTS.md: Part 1, Rule 1` (64-bit precision / RTE — all rendering paths)
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** `WebGPUEdgeVisibilityEmitter.ts` declares single-precision float vertex attributes:
  ```wgsl
  @location(0) position: vec3<f32>,
  @location(4) otherPos: vec3<f32>,
  ```
  And executes raw `camera.modelViewProjection * vec4<f32>(input.position, 1.0)`.
  In `WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:8754-8757`, the codebase contains an explicit admission:
  ```ts
  // RTE is not applied here, which is acceptable at typical distances.
  ```
  This is a direct violation of Fork Charter Rule 1. In planetary-scale ECEF coordinate spaces ($R \approx 6.378 \times 10^6\text{ m}$), 32-bit floats have only 24 bits of mantissa, yielding precision loss of $\pm 0.5\text{ m}$ to $\pm 1.0\text{ m}$.
  When `WebGPUEdgeVisibilityEmitter.ts:171-184` computes screen-space quad expansion vectors via `dirNDC = normalize(otherNDC - curNDC)`, sub-meter truncation causes erratic sign flips in `perpNDC`, causing wide-line triangles to invert, collapse, and jitter violently.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** 3D Tilesets rendered in global coordinates (e.g. Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles or Cesium World Terrain) with edge visibility enabled exhibit vibrating, torn, and discontinuous edge quads that jitter across frames whenever the camera moves.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Split edge positions into `positionHigh`/`positionLow` and `otherPosHigh`/`otherPosLow` attributes in `EdgeGeometry`. Pack uniform camera high/low coordinates into `EdgeUniforms`, and compute clip positions using `mvpRelativeToEye * (translateRelativeToEye(posHigh, posLow, cameraHigh, cameraLow))`.

### C-403. HTMLVideoElement Zero-Dimension Nullish Coalescing Defect Causing GPUValidationError and Silent Video Dropping
* **Target Subsystems:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUImageUpload.ts:197-200, 203-216`, `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/Stubs/WebGLStubTexture.ts:880-890, 1078-1088`
* **Vulnerability Mechanism:** In HTML5 DOM standards, `HTMLVideoElement` inherits `width` and `height` integer IDL attributes reflecting the HTML tag attributes; when created dynamically (e.g. `document.createElement('video')`) without explicit CSS/DOM dimension attributes, `video.width === 0` and `video.height === 0`, while the media stream's intrinsic dimensions reside in `video.videoWidth` and `video.videoHeight`.
  In `WebGPUImageUpload.ts:197-200`:
  ```typescript
  const w = (decoded as { width?: number; videoWidth?: number }).width;
  const h = (decoded as { height?: number; videoHeight?: number }).height;
  width = w ?? (decoded as HTMLVideoElement).videoWidth;
  height = h ?? (decoded as HTMLVideoElement).videoHeight;
  ```
  And in `WebGLStubTexture.ts:886-887` & `1084-1085`:
  ```typescript
  width = sized.width ?? sized.videoWidth ?? 0;
  height = sized.height ?? sized.videoHeight ?? 0;
  ```
  Because `0` is a valid number, JavaScript nullish coalescing (`??`) evaluates `0 ?? 1920` to `0` instead of falling back to `videoWidth`.
  In `WebGPUImageUpload.ts:215`, `{ width: 0, height: 0 }` is passed into `device.queue.copyExternalImageToTexture(...)`. Under the WebGPU Specification (§14.2), `copySize.width` and `copySize.height` must be $> 0$; passing 0 immediately triggers an asynchronous `GPUValidationError` on the `GPUDevice`.
  In `WebGLStubTexture.ts:890` & `1088`, `if (width <= 0 || height <= 0) return;` evaluates to true, silently dropping the video frame completely and skipping texture allocation and upload. Furthermore, if a developer sets `<video width="320" height="180">` for layout but streams a 1080p video, `w` resolves to `320`, corrupting texture coordinates and clipping the frame.
* **Real-World Failure Scenario:** Any user creating a video overlay on terrain or material (`material.uniforms.image = videoElement`) using standard JavaScript (`document.createElement('video')`) experiences either an uncaptured WebGPU validation crash or a completely blank/default white texture.
* **Architectural Remediation:** Explicitly check `videoWidth` and `videoHeight` first, mirroring `Texture.js:426-428`:
  ```typescript
  let width: number;
  let height: number;
  if ("videoWidth" in decoded && typeof decoded.videoWidth === "number" && decoded.videoWidth > 0) {
    width = decoded.videoWidth;
    height = decoded.videoHeight;
  } else if ("naturalWidth" in decoded && typeof decoded.naturalWidth === "number" && decoded.naturalWidth > 0) {
    width = decoded.naturalWidth;
    height = decoded.naturalHeight;
  } else {
    width = decoded.width ?? 0;
    height = decoded.height ?? 0;
  }
  ```
